# Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence v2 (ARC-AGI-2)

This repository contains the ARC-AGI-2 task data (ARC-AGI-1 can be found [here](https://github.com/fchollet/arc-agi)).

*"ARC can be seen as a general artificial intelligence benchmark, as a program synthesis benchmark, or as a psychometric intelligence test. It is targeted at both humans and artificially intelligent systems that aim at emulating a human-like form of general fluid intelligence."*

A foundational description of the dataset, its goals, and its underlying logic, can be found in: [On the Measure of Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01547), the [ARC-AGI-2 Presentation](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1hQrGh5YI6MK3PalQYSQs4CQERrYBQZue8PBLjjHIMgI/edit?usp=sharing) and [ARC-AGI-2 Technical Report](http://arcprize.org/blog/arc-agi-2-technical-report)

## Dataset composition

ARC-AGI-2 contains 1,000 public training tasks and 120 public evaluation tasks.

The training tasks are intended to demonstrate the task format and the Core Knowledge priors used by ARC-AGI. They can be used for training AI models.
The public evaluation tasks are intended for testing AI models that have never seen these tasks before. Average human performance on these tasks in our test sample was 66%.

ARC-AGI-2 also features two private test sets not included in the repo:

- A semi-private set intended for testing remotely-hosted commercial models with low leakage probability. It is calibrated to be the same human-facing difficulty as the public evaluation set.
- A fully-private set intended for testing self-contained models during the ARC Prize competition, with near-zeo leakage probability. It is also calibrated to be the same difficulty.

This multi-tiered structure allows for both open research and a secure, high-stakes competition.

## Task success criterion

A test-taker is said to solve a task when, upon seeing the task for the first time, they are able to produce the correct output grid for *all* test inputs in the task (this includes picking the dimensions of the output grid). For each test input, the test-taker is allowed 2 trials (this holds for all test-takers, either humans or AI).

## Task file format

The `data` directory contains two subdirectories:

- `data/training`: contains the task files for training (1000 tasks). Use these to prototype your algorithm or to train your algorithm to acquire ARC-relevant cognitive priors. This set combines tasks from ARC-AGI-1 as well as new tasks.
- `data/evaluation`: contains the task files for evaluation (120 tasks). Use these to evaluate your final algorithm. To ensure fair evaluation results, do not leak information from the evaluation set into your algorithm (e.g. by looking at the evaluation tasks yourself during development, or by repeatedly modifying an algorithm while using its evaluation score as feedback). Each task in `evaluation` has been solved by a minimum of 2 people (many tasks were solved by more) in 2 attempts or less in a controlled test.

The tasks are stored in JSON format. Each task JSON file contains a dictionary with two fields:

- `"train"`: demonstration input/output pairs. It is a list of "pairs" (typically 3 pairs).
- `"test"`: test input/output pairs. It is a list of "pairs" (typically 1-2 pair).

A "pair" is a dictionary with two fields:

- `"input"`: the input "grid" for the pair.
- `"output"`: the output "grid" for the pair.

A "grid" is a rectangular matrix (list of lists) of integers between 0 and 9 (inclusive). The smallest possible grid size is 1x1 and the largest is 30x30.

When looking at a task, a test-taker has access to inputs & outputs of the demonstration pairs, plus the input(s) of the test pair(s). The goal is to construct the output grid(s) corresponding to the test input grid(s), using 3 trials for each test input. "Constructing the output grid" involves picking the height and width of the output grid, then filling each cell in the grid with a symbol (integer between 0 and 9, which are visualized as colors). Only *exact* solutions (all cells match the expected answer) can be said to be correct.


## Usage of the testing interface

You can view tasks on [ARCPrize.org/play](https://arcprize.org/play) or clone the [ARC-AGI-1 testing interface](https://github.com/fchollet/ARC-AGI/tree/master/apps). Open it in a web browser (Chrome recommended). It will prompt you to select a task JSON file.

After loading a task, you will enter the test space, which looks like this:

![test space](https://arc-benchmark.s3.amazonaws.com/figs/arc_test_space.png)

On the left, you will see the input/output pairs demonstrating the nature of the task. In the middle, you will see the current test input grid. On the right, you will see the controls you can use to construct the corresponding output grid.

You have access to the following tools:

### Grid controls

- Resize: input a grid size (e.g. "10x20" or "4x4") and click "Resize". This preserves existing grid content (in the top left corner).
- Copy from input: copy the input grid to the output grid. This is useful for tasks where the output consists of some modification of the input.
- Reset grid: fill the grid with 0s.

### Symbol controls

- Edit: select a color (symbol) from the color picking bar, then click on a cell to set its color.
- Select: click and drag on either the output grid or the input grid to select cells.
    - After selecting cells on the output grid, you can select a color from the color picking to set the color of the selected cells. This is useful to draw solid rectangles or lines.
    - After selecting cells on either the input grid or the output grid, you can press C to copy their content. After copying, you can select a cell on the output grid and press "V" to paste the copied content. You should select the cell in the top left corner of the zone you want to paste into.
- Floodfill: click on a cell from the output grid to color all connected cells to the selected color. "Connected cells" are contiguous cells with the same color.

### Answer validation

When your output grid is ready, click the green "Submit!" button to check your answer. We do not enforce the 2-trials rule.

After you've obtained the correct answer for the current test input grid, you can switch to the next test input grid for the task using the "Next test input" button (if there is any available; most tasks only have one test input).

When you're done with a task, use the "load task" button to open a new task.

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List


class ArchitectureValidator:
    """
    Validates the HERCULE project
    architecture.

    Checks:

    • Required directories
    • Required files
    • Package structure
    • Overall integrity
    """

    REQUIRED_DIRECTORIES = [

        "abilities",
        "agents",
        "boot",
        "brain",
        "cognition",
        "communication",
        "developer_tools",
        "engineering",
        "intelligence",
        "kernel",
        "knowledge",
        "memory",
        "models",
        "orchestrator",
        "perception",
        "plugins",
        "robotics",
        "runtime",
        "security",
        "simulation",
        "system",

    ]

    REQUIRED_FILES = [

        "boot.py",
        "README.md",
        "requirements.txt",
        "pyproject.toml",

    ]

    def __init__(
        self,
        project_root: str | Path = ".",
    ) -> None:

        self.project_root = Path(
            project_root
        ).resolve()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def validate(self) -> Dict:

        missing_dirs = self._check_directories()

        missing_files = self._check_files()

        success = (

            len(missing_dirs) == 0

            and

            len(missing_files) == 0

        )

        return {

            "success": success,

            "project_root": str(
                self.project_root
            ),

            "missing_directories":
                missing_dirs,

            "missing_files":
                missing_files,

            "checked_directories":
                len(self.REQUIRED_DIRECTORIES),

            "checked_files":
                len(self.REQUIRED_FILES),

        }

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def _check_directories(
        self,
    ) -> List[str]:

        missing = []

        for directory in self.REQUIRED_DIRECTORIES:

            path = self.project_root / directory

            if not path.exists():

                missing.append(directory)

        return missing

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def _check_files(
        self,
    ) -> List[str]:

        missing = []

        for filename in self.REQUIRED_FILES:

            path = self.project_root / filename

            if not path.exists():

                missing.append(filename)

        return missing

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def print_report(self):

        report = self.validate()

        print("\n========== Architecture ==========\n")

        print(
            f"Project : {report['project_root']}"
        )

        print(
            f"Status  : "
            f"{'PASSED' if report['success'] else 'FAILED'}"
        )

        print()

        if report["missing_directories"]:

            print("Missing Directories:")

            for item in report[
                "missing_directories"
            ]:

                print(f" - {item}")

        if report["missing_files"]:

            print("\nMissing Files:")

            for item in report[
                "missing_files"
            ]:

                print(f" - {item}")

        if report["success"]:

            print(
                "Architecture validation successful."
            )

        print(
            "\n==================================\n"
        )

import time
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict


class Benchmark:
    """
    Measures the performance of HERCULE
    components.

    Benchmarks:

    • Startup time
    • Function execution
    • Average runtime
    • Multiple iterations
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:

        self.results: Dict[str, Dict] = {}

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def run(
        self,
        name: str,
        function: Callable[..., Any],
        *args,
        iterations: int = 1,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> Dict:

        durations = []

        output = None

        for _ in range(iterations):

            start = time.perf_counter()

            output = function(
                *args,
                **kwargs,
            )

            end = time.perf_counter()

            durations.append(
                end - start
            )

        report = {

            "iterations": iterations,

            "minimum": round(
                min(durations),
                6,
            ),

            "maximum": round(
                max(durations),
                6,
            ),

            "average": round(
                sum(durations) / len(durations),
                6,
            ),

            "last_result": output,

        }

        self.results[name] = report

        return report

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def get_result(
        self,
        name: str,
    ) -> Dict | None:

        return self.results.get(name)

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def get_all_results(
        self,
    ) -> Dict[str, Dict]:

        return self.results

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def clear(self) -> None:

        self.results.clear()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def print_report(self) -> None:

        print("\n========== Benchmark ==========\n")

        if not self.results:

            print("No benchmarks executed.\n")
            return

        for name, result in self.results.items():

            print(f"Component : {name}")

            print(
                f"Iterations : {result['iterations']}"
            )

            print(
                f"Average    : {result['average']} sec"
            )

            print(
                f"Minimum    : {result['minimum']} sec"
            )

            print(
                f"Maximum    : {result['maximum']} sec"
            )

            print()

        print("===============================\n")

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict

from developer_tools.static_analysis import StaticAnalyzer
from developer_tools.duplicate_detector import DuplicateDetector
from developer_tools.dead_code_detector import DeadCodeDetector
from developer_tools.circular_dependency import CircularDependencyDetector
from developer_tools.package_validator import PackageValidator


class CodeQuality:
    """
    Computes an overall quality score
    for the HERCULE project.

    Score Range:
        90-100 : Excellent
        75-89  : Good
        60-74  : Fair
        <60    : Needs Improvement
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        project_root: str | Path = ".",
    ) -> None:

        self.project_root = Path(project_root).resolve()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def evaluate(self) -> Dict:

        static = StaticAnalyzer(
            self.project_root
        ).analyze()

        duplicate = DuplicateDetector(
            self.project_root
        ).scan()

        dead = DeadCodeDetector(
            self.project_root
        ).analyze()

        circular = CircularDependencyDetector(
            self.project_root
        ).analyze()

        packages = PackageValidator(
            self.project_root
        ).validate()

        score = 100

        score -= len(
            duplicate["duplicates"]
        ) * 2

        score -= len(
            dead["unused"]
        )

        score -= circular[
            "cycle_count"
        ] * 5

        score -= len(
            packages["missing_init"]
        ) * 2

        score = max(0, score)

        if score >= 90:

            rating = "Excellent"

        elif score >= 75:

            rating = "Good"

        elif score >= 60:

            rating = "Fair"

        else:

            rating = "Needs Improvement"

        return {

            "score": score,

            "rating": rating,

            "summary": {

                "python_files":
                    static.get(
                        "python_files",
                        0,
                    ),

                "duplicates":
                    duplicate[
                        "duplicate_groups"
                    ],

                "dead_code":
                    len(
                        dead["unused"]
                    ),

                "circular_dependencies":
                    circular[
                        "cycle_count"
                    ],

                "missing_init":
                    len(
                        packages[
                            "missing_init"
                        ]
                    ),

            },

        }

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def print_report(self) -> None:

        report = self.evaluate()

        print(
            "\n========== HERCULE Code Quality ==========\n"
        )

        print(
            f"Quality Score : {report['score']}/100"
        )

        print(
            f"Rating        : {report['rating']}"
        )

        print("\nMetrics\n")

        for key, value in report[
            "summary"
        ].items():

            print(
                f"{key:<25}: {value}"
            )

        print(
            "\n==========================================\n"
        )

import ast
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List


class ImportChecker:
    """
    Scans every Python file in the project and
    validates import statements.

    Checks:

    • Invalid imports
    • Missing modules
    • Syntax errors
    • Import statistics
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        project_root: str | Path = ".",
    ) -> None:

        self.project_root = Path(
            project_root
        ).resolve()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def check(self) -> Dict:

        files = list(
            self.project_root.rglob("*.py")
        )

        scanned = 0

        errors = []

        imports = 0

        for file in files:

            scanned += 1

            result = self._scan_file(file)

            imports += result["imports"]

            errors.extend(result["errors"])

        return {

            "success":
                len(errors) == 0,

            "files_scanned":
                scanned,

            "imports_found":
                imports,

            "errors":
                errors,

        }

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def _scan_file(
        self,
        file: Path,
    ) -> Dict:

        found_imports = 0

        errors = []

        try:

            source = file.read_text(
                encoding="utf-8"
            )

            tree = ast.parse(source)

            for node in ast.walk(tree):

                if isinstance(
                    node,
                    (
                        ast.Import,
                        ast.ImportFrom,
                    ),
                ):

                    found_imports += 1

        except SyntaxError as exc:

            errors.append({

                "file":
                    str(file.relative_to(
                        self.project_root
                    )),

                "line":
                    exc.lineno,

                "message":
                    str(exc),

            })

        except Exception as exc:

            errors.append({

                "file":
                    str(file.relative_to(
                        self.project_root
                    )),

                "line":
                    None,

                "message":
                    str(exc),

            })

        return {

            "imports":
                found_imports,

            "errors":
                errors,

        }

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List


class ProjectScanner:
    """
    Scans the HERCULE project directory and
    indexes all files and folders.

    Collects:

    • Directory structure
    • Python files
    • File sizes
    • File extensions
    • Statistics
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        project_root: str | Path = ".",
    ) -> None:

        self.project_root = Path(
            project_root
        ).resolve()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def scan(self) -> Dict:

        report = {

            "root": str(self.project_root),

            "directories": [],

            "files": [],

            "python_files": [],

            "extensions": {},

            "total_directories": 0,

            "total_files": 0,

        }

        for path in self.project_root.rglob("*"):

            if path.is_dir():

                report["directories"].append(

                    str(
                        path.relative_to(
                            self.project_root
                        )
                    )

                )

                report["total_directories"] += 1

            elif path.is_file():

                relative = str(

                    path.relative_to(
                        self.project_root
                    )

                )

                extension = path.suffix.lower()

                report["files"].append({

                    "path": relative,

                    "extension": extension,

                    "size": path.stat().st_size,

                })

                report["total_files"] += 1

                report["extensions"][extension] = (

                    report["extensions"].get(

                        extension,

                        0,

                    )

                    + 1

                )

                if extension == ".py":

                    report["python_files"].append(

                        relative

                    )

        return report

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def print_report(self) -> None:

        report = self.scan()

        print("\n========== Project Scanner ==========\n")

        print(
            f"Root         : {report['root']}"
        )

        print(
            f"Directories  : {report['total_directories']}"
        )

        print(
            f"Files        : {report['total_files']}"
        )

        print(
            f"Python Files : {len(report['python_files'])}"
        )

        print("\nExtensions:\n")

        for ext, count in sorted(

            report["extensions"].items()

        ):

            label = ext if ext else "<no extension>"

            print(

                f"{label:<15} {count}"

            )

        print(

            "\n=====================================\n"

        )

import json

class ReportGenerator:
    """
    Generates a comprehensive project report
    from all developer toolkit modules.

    Supported Formats

    • Console
    • JSON
    • Markdown

    The report is read-only and never modifies
    the HERCULE project.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:

        self.sections: Dict[str, Any] = {}

        self.timestamp = datetime.now()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def add_section(

        self,

        name: str,

        data: Dict,

    ) -> None:

        self.sections[name] = data

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def overall_score(self) -> int:

        score = 100

        for section in self.sections.values():

            if not isinstance(section, dict):
                continue

            score -= section.get("errors", 0)

            score -= section.get("warnings", 0)

            score -= section.get("critical", 0) * 5

        return max(0, score)

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def readiness(self) -> str:

        score = self.overall_score()

        if score >= 95:
            return "Production Ready"

        if score >= 85:
            return "Release Candidate"

        if score >= 70:
            return "Development Stable"

        if score >= 50:
            return "Needs Improvements"

        return "Not Ready"

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def generate(self) -> Dict:

        return {

            "timestamp":

                self.timestamp.isoformat(),

            "overall_score":

                self.overall_score(),

            "status":

                self.readiness(),

            "sections":

                self.sections,

        }

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def export_json(

        self,

        filename: str | Path,

    ) -> None:

        Path(filename).write_text(

            json.dumps(

                self.generate(),

                indent=4,

            ),

            encoding="utf-8",

        )

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def export_markdown(

        self,

        filename: str | Path,

    ) -> None:

        report = self.generate()

        lines = [

            "# HERCULE Project Report",

            "",

            f"Generated : {report['timestamp']}",

            "",

            f"Overall Score : {report['overall_score']}/100",

            f"Status : {report['status']}",

            "",

            "---",

            "",

        ]

        for section, values in report["sections"].items():

            lines.append(f"## {section}")

            lines.append("")

            if isinstance(values, dict):

                for key, value in values.items():

                    lines.append(f"- **{key}** : {value}")

            else:

                lines.append(str(values))

            lines.append("")

        Path(filename).write_text(

            "\n".join(lines),

            encoding="utf-8",

        )

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def print_report(self) -> None:

        report = self.generate()

        print("\n========== HERCULE PROJECT REPORT ==========\n")

        print(

        print(

            f"Status    : "

            f"{report['status']}"

        )

        print("\nSections\n")

        for section in report["sections"]:

    • Startup
    • Initialization
    • Request processing
    • Response generation
    • Shutdown
    """

                self.runtime.start()

            report["startup"] = True

            if hasattr(self.runtime, "process"):

                result = self.runtime.process(
                    "Hello HERCULE"

                    report["response"] = True

            elif hasattr(self.runtime, "execute"):

                result = self.runtime.execute(
                    "Hello HERCULE"
                )

                report["request"] = True

                if result is not None:

                    report["response"] = True

            # Shutdown

            if hasattr(self.runtime, "shutdown"):

                self.runtime.shutdown()

            elif hasattr(self.runtime, "stop"):

                self.runtime.stop()

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List


class ImportRepair:
    """
    Repairs broken Python imports.

    Features
    --------
    • Detect invalid imports
    • Replace outdated imports
    • Dry-run support
    • Detailed repair report

    NOTE:
    No file is modified unless
    dry_run=False.
    """

    def __init__(

        self,

        project_root: str | Path = ".",

    ) -> None:

        self.project_root = Path(
            project_root
        ).resolve()

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def repair(

        self,

        replacements: Dict[str, str],

        dry_run: bool = True,

    ) -> Dict:

        repaired_files: List[str] = []

        repaired_imports = 0

        for file in self.project_root.rglob("*.py"):

            try:

                original = file.read_text(
                    encoding="utf-8"
                )

                updated = original

                for old, new in replacements.items():

                    pattern = rf"\b{re.escape(old)}\b"

                    updated = re.sub(
                        pattern,
                        new,
                        updated,
                    )

                if updated != original:

                    repaired_imports += 1

                    repaired_files.append(

                        str(
                            file.relative_to(
                                self.project_root
                            )
                        )

                    )

                    if not dry_run:

                        file.write_text(
                            updated,
                            encoding="utf-8",
                        )

            except Exception:

                continue

        return {

            "dry_run":

                dry_run,

            "files_modified":

                len(repaired_files),

            "imports_repaired":

                repaired_imports,

            "modified_files":

                repaired_files,

        }

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def print_report(

        self,

        report: Dict,

    ) -> None:

        print(
            "\n========== Import Repair ==========\n"
        )

        print(
            f"Dry Run          : {report['dry_run']}"
        )

        print(
            f"Files Modified   : {report['files_modified']}"
        )

        print(
            f"Imports Repaired : {report['imports_repaired']}"
        )

        if report["modified_files"]:

            print("\nAffected Files\n")

            for file in report["modified_files"]:

                print(f" • {file}")

        else:

            print(
                "\nNo import issues found."
            )

        print(
            "\n===================================\n"
        )

    preserve_docstrings: bool = True

    compatibility_mode: bool = True
    minimal_changes: bool = True
    create_wrappers: bool = True

    analyze_dependencies: bool = True
    analyze_interfaces: bool = True
    analyze_imports: bool = True
    analyze_runtime: bool = True

    # Logging
    verbose: bool = True
    save_reports: bool = True

    # File Types
    supported_extensions: tuple = field(
        default_factory=lambda: (
            ".py",
        )
    )

    # Ignore folders
    ignored_directories: tuple = field(
        default_factory=lambda: (
            "__pycache__",
            ".git",
            ".idea",
            ".vscode",
            "venv",
            ".venv",
            "build",
            "dist",
        )
    )

    def backup_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Returns backup folder.

        Frozen (installed) apps must never write into Program Files:
        dev-tool backups redirect into %LOCALAPPDATA%\\HERCULE.
        """
        try:
            from system.paths import is_frozen, user_data_dir
            if is_frozen():
                return user_data_dir() / "smart_repair_backups"
        except Exception:
            pass
        return self.project_root / self.backup_directory

    def is_supported(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        """
        Checks whether a file is supported.
        """
        return path.suffix in self.supported_extensions

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

from .repair_config import RepairConfig
from .repair_history import RepairHistory
from .repair_report import RepairReport


class RepairEngine:
    """
    Central engine responsible for coordinating
    analysis, repair, validation and rollback.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: Optional[RepairConfig] = None):

        self.config = config or RepairConfig()

        history_file = (
            self.config.backup_path() /
            "repair_history.json"
        )

        self.history = RepairHistory(history_file)

        self.report = RepairReport()

        self.analyzers = []

        self.patchers = []

        self.validators = []

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def register_analyzer(self, analyzer):

        self.analyzers.append(analyzer)

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def register_patcher(self, patcher):

        self.patchers.append(patcher)

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def register_validator(self, validator):

        self.validators.append(validator)

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def analyze(self, file_path: Path) -> List[Dict]:

        issues = []

        for analyzer in self.analyzers:

            try:

                result = analyzer.scan(file_path)

                if result:

                    issues.extend(result)

            except Exception as exc:

                self.report.add(

                    severity="WARNING",

                    file=str(file_path),

                    issue=str(exc),

                    solution="Analyzer execution failed",

                    status="FAILED",

                )

        return issues

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def create_plan(self, issues):

        plan = []

        for issue in issues:

            plan.append(

                {

                    "issue": issue,

                    "status": "PENDING"

                }

            )

        return plan

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def repair(self, file_path: Path):

        issues = self.analyze(file_path)

        plan = self.create_plan(issues)

        return plan

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def validate(self, file_path: Path):

        results = []

        for validator in self.validators:

            try:

                results.append(

                    validator.validate(file_path)

                )

            except Exception as exc:

                results.append(

                    {

                        "validator":

                            validator.__class__.__name__,

                        "success": False,

                        "reason": str(exc),

                    }

                )

        return results

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def record_success(

        self,

        file_path,

        issue,

        action,

        backup=None,

    ):

        self.history.record(

            file_path=file_path,

            issue=issue,

            action=action,

            status="SUCCESS",

            backup=backup,

        )

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def record_failure(

        self,

        file_path,

        issue,

        action,

        backup=None,

    ):

        self.history.record(

            file_path=file_path,

            issue=issue,

            action=action,

            status="FAILED",

            backup=backup,

        )

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def clear(self):

        self.report.entries.clear()

from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
import json


class RepairHistory:
    """
    Stores every repair operation performed by
    the Smart Repair Engine.
    """

    def __init__(self, history_file: Path):

        self.history_file = Path(history_file)

        self.history_file.parent.mkdir(
            parents=True,
            exist_ok=True
        )

        if not self.history_file.exists():

            self.history_file.write_text(
                "[]",
                encoding="utf-8"
            )

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def _load(self):

        try:

            return json.loads(
                self.history_file.read_text(
                    encoding="utf-8"
                )
            )

        except Exception:

            return []

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def _save(self, history):

        self.history_file.write_text(

            json.dumps(
                history,
                indent=4
            ),

            encoding="utf-8"

        )

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def record(

        self,

        file_path: str,

        issue: str,

        action: str,

        status: str,

        backup: str | None = None

    ):

        history = self._load()

        history.append(

            {

                "timestamp":

                    datetime.now().isoformat(),

                "file":

                    file_path,

                "issue":

                    issue,

                "action":

                    action,

                "status":

                    status,

                "backup":

                    backup

            }

        )

        return self._load()[-count:]

        self._save([])

"""
HERCULE Smart Repair Engine

Repair Report
"""


from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime


class RepairReport:

    """
    Creates human-readable repair reports.
    """

    def __init__(self):

        self.entries = []

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def add(

        self,

        severity,

        file,

        issue,

        solution,

        status

    ):

        self.entries.append(

            {

                "severity": severity,

                "file": file,

                "issue": issue,

                "solution": solution,

                "status": status

            }

        )

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def summary(self):

        return {

            "total": len(self.entries),

            "critical":

                sum(
                    1
                    for e in self.entries
                    if e["severity"] == "CRITICAL"
                ),

            "warnings":

                sum(
                    1
                    for e in self.entries
                    if e["severity"] == "WARNING"
                ),

            "fixed":

                sum(
                    1
                    for e in self.entries
                    if e["status"] == "FIXED"
                ),

            "failed":

                sum(
                    1
                    for e in self.entries
                    if e["status"] == "FAILED"
                )

        }

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def save(self, filename):

        filename = Path(filename)

        filename.parent.mkdir(

            parents=True,

            exist_ok=True

        )

        report = []

        report.append(
            "# HERCULE Smart Repair Report\n"
        )

        report.append(

            f"Generated: "

            f"{datetime.now().isoformat()}\n"

        )

        report.append("---\n")

        summary = self.summary()

        report.append(
            f"Total Issues : {summary['total']}\n"
        )

        report.append(
            f"Critical : {summary['critical']}\n"
        )

        report.append(
            f"Warnings : {summary['warnings']}\n"
        )

        report.append(
            f"Fixed : {summary['fixed']}\n"
        )

        report.append(
            f"Failed : {summary['failed']}\n\n"
        )

        for item in self.entries:

            report.append(
                "---------------------------------\n"
            )

            report.append(
                f"Severity : {item['severity']}\n"
            )

            report.append(
                f"File : {item['file']}\n"
            )

            report.append(
                f"Issue : {item['issue']}\n"
            )

            report.append(
                f"Solution : {item['solution']}\n"
            )

            report.append(
                f"Status : {item['status']}\n\n"
            )

        filename.write_text(

            "".join(report),

            encoding="utf-8"

        )

"""
HERCULE Smart Repair Engine

Smart Repair Manager

Main entry point for automatic project repair.
"""


from pathlib import Path
from typing import List

from .repair_engine import RepairEngine
from .repair_config import RepairConfig

# Built-in analyzers
from .analyzers.import_analyzer import ImportAnalyzer
from .analyzers.interface_analyzer import InterfaceAnalyzer
from .analyzers.syntax_analyzer import SyntaxAnalyzer
from .analyzers.placeholder_analyzer import PlaceholderAnalyzer
from .analyzers.dependency_analyzer import DependencyAnalyzer
from .analyzers.runtime_analyzer import RuntimeAnalyzer

# Built-in validators
from .validation.import_validator import ImportValidator
from .validation.interface_validator import InterfaceValidator
from .validation.runtime_validator import RuntimeValidator
from .validation.project_validator import ProjectValidator

# Backup
from .backup.backup_manager import BackupManager

# Rollback
from .backup.rollback_manager import RollbackManager


class SmartRepairManager:
    """
    Main controller of the Smart Repair Engine.

    Responsibilities
    ----------------

    • Scan project

    • Analyze problems

    • Backup files

    • Repair safely

    • Validate repairs

    • Rollback failures

    • Generate reports
    """

    def __init__(self, config: RepairConfig | None = None):

        self.config = config or RepairConfig()

        self.engine = RepairEngine(self.config)

        self.backup = BackupManager(self.config)

        self.rollback = RollbackManager(self.config)

        self._register_defaults()

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def _register_defaults(self):

        # ---------- Analyzers ----------

        self.engine.register_analyzer(
            SyntaxAnalyzer()
        )

        self.engine.register_analyzer(
            ImportAnalyzer()
        )

        self.engine.register_analyzer(
            InterfaceAnalyzer()
        )

        self.engine.register_analyzer(
            DependencyAnalyzer()
        )

        self.engine.register_analyzer(
            PlaceholderAnalyzer()
        )

        self.engine.register_analyzer(
            RuntimeAnalyzer()
        )

        # ---------- Validators ----------

        self.engine.register_validator(
            ImportValidator()
        )

        self.engine.register_validator(
            InterfaceValidator()
        )

        self.engine.register_validator(
            RuntimeValidator()
        )

        self.engine.register_validator(
            ProjectValidator()
        )

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def scan_file(self, file_path: Path):

        return self.engine.analyze(file_path)

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def repair_file(self, file_path: Path):

        print(f"\nScanning {file_path}")

        issues = self.engine.analyze(file_path)

        if not issues:

            print("No issues detected.")

            return True

        print(f"Found {len(issues)} issue(s).")

        backup = self.backup.create_backup(file_path)

        try:

            for issue in issues:

                print(

                    f"Repairing: "

                    f"{issue.get('type','Unknown')}"

                )

                # Patchers will be executed here
                # in Batch 3

            results = self.engine.validate(file_path)

            failed = any(
                not r.get("success", True)
                for r in results
            )

            if failed:

                raise RuntimeError(
                    "Validation failed."
                )

            self.engine.record_success(

                str(file_path),

                "Automatic repair",

                "Applied",

                str(backup)

            )

            print("Repair successful.")

            return True

        except Exception as exc:

            print(

                f"Repair failed: {exc}"

            )

            self.rollback.restore(

                backup,

                file_path

            )

            self.engine.record_failure(

                str(file_path),

                str(exc),

                "Rollback",

                str(backup)

            )

            return False

    # -------------------------------------------------

    def repair_project(self):

        root = self.config.project_root

        repaired = 0

        scanned = 0

        for file in root.rglob("*.py"):

            if any(

                folder in file.parts

                for folder in

                self.config.ignored_directories

            ):

                continue

            scanned += 1

            if self.repair_file(file):

                repaired += 1

        print("\n========== SUMMARY ==========")

        print(f"Files scanned : {scanned}")

        print(f"Files repaired: {repaired}")

        print("=============================")

"""
HERCULE Smart Repair Engine

Backup Manager
"""


import shutil
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from ..repair_config import RepairConfig


class BackupManager:
    """
    Creates timestamped backups before
    any repair operation.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: RepairConfig):

        self.config = config

        self.root = self.config.backup_path()

        self.root.mkdir(
            parents=True,
            exist_ok=True
        )

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def create_backup(self, file_path: Path) -> Path:

        file_path = Path(file_path)

        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime(
            "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"
        )

        relative = file_path.relative_to(
            self.config.project_root
        )

        backup = (
            self.root /
            timestamp /
            relative
        )

        backup.parent.mkdir(
            parents=True,
            exist_ok=True
        )

        shutil.copy2(file_path, backup)

        return backup

from __future__ import annotations
"""
Restore Manager

Allows restoring backups manually.
"""


import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from ..repair_config import RepairConfig


class RestoreManager:

    def __init__(self, config: RepairConfig):

        self.config = config

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def restore(

        self,

        backup: Path,

        destination: Path

    ) -> bool:

        backup = Path(backup)

        destination = Path(destination)

        if not backup.exists():

            return False

        destination.parent.mkdir(

            parents=True,

            exist_ok=True

        )

        shutil.copy2(

            backup,

            destination

        )

        return True

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def available_backups(self):

        backups = []

        root = self.config.backup_path()

        if not root.exists():

            return backups

        for file in root.rglob("*.py"):

            backups.append(file)

        return sorted(backups)

from ..repair_config import RepairConfig


class RollbackManager:

    """
    Restores the original file if a repair
    fails validation.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: RepairConfig):

        self.config = config

    # --------------------------------------------------

    def restore(

        self,

        backup_file: Path,

        target_file: Path

    ) -> bool:

        backup_file = Path(backup_file)

        target_file = Path(target_file)

        if not backup_file.exists():

            return False

        shutil.copy2(

            backup_file,

            target_file

        )

        return True

# High-level Architecture Diagram

This diagram shows major components and their responsibilities.

```mermaid
graph TB
  User((User)) -->|text/voice| Interface
  Interface --> Orchestrator[Orchestrator / Frontend]
  Orchestrator --> AgentMgr[Agent Manager / Scheduler]
  AgentMgr --> Agent[Agents]
  Agent -->|read/write| Memory[Memory / Vector Store]
  Agent --> Models[Model Layer]
  Models --> Embeddings[Embedding Models]
  Models --> LLMs[LLMs (local/remote)]
  Orchestrator --> Perception[Perception (Vision/ASR/TTS)]
  Agent --> SystemCtrl[System Control Adapters]
  Monitoring -->|metrics/logs| Observability[Observability & Security]
  AgentMgr --> Planner[Planner / Decision Engine]
  Planner --> Executor[Executor / Tool Adapters]

  style Interface fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
  style AgentMgr fill:#efe,stroke:#333
  style Memory fill:#ffd,stroke:#333
```

## Component Responsibilities
- Interface: Accepts user input (text, voice, GUI) and displays responses/status.
- Orchestrator: Routes requests, enforces policies, aggregates telemetry.
- Agent Manager: Registers, schedules and supervises agents; provides lifecycle APIs.
- Agents: Domain-specialized workers (research, coding, vision, system control).
- Memory: Persistent and vectorized memory with ranking and retrieval APIs.
- Models: Hosts LLMs and embedding models; provides routing and fallback.
- Perception: ASR/TTS, OCR, vision preprocessing and annotation.
- Planner/Executor: Converts goals into plans and executes via tool adapters.
- System Control: Safe adapters for OS-level actions with permission checks.
- Observability: Logs, metrics, security monitoring, and audit trails.

# HERCULE Request Lifecycle Architecture

## Paths

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT([INPUT cli.handle_line]) --> CLASSIFY[boot.classify_request\nrouter.classify_detailed + capability inference]
    CLASSIFY -->|CHAT + no capabilities| QUESTION[QUESTION\nBrain.think → ModelManager → response]
    CLASSIFY -->|slash command / capabilities / subsystem intent| GOAL[GOAL\nBrain.run_cycle]
    QUESTION --> QMEM[episodic conversation record\nbest-effort]
    QMEM --> QRESP([RESPONSE\nno task, no plan, no healing])
    GOAL --> INTENT[INTENT → CONTEXT → MEMORY/KNOWLEDGE]
    INTENT --> REASON[REASONING\nReasoner + LLM genuine reasoning]
    REASON --> PLAN[PLAN\ncreate_capable_plan\ncontract: step_id + goal + required_capabilities + verification_criteria]
    PLAN -->|contract invalid| FAIL1([FAILED\nMISSING_CAPABILITIES / MISSING_VERIFICATION])
    PLAN --> TVAL[PLAN VALIDATION\nvalidate_plan: registry, policy, deps, verification]
    TVAL --> TCREATE[TaskManager create/queue/start\nidempotent + resume-safe]
    TCREATE --> LOOP[AutonomousLoop\ncapability resolution → tool matching → policy → execution → observation → verification]
    LOOP -->|execution fail + replans left| REPLAN[bounded replan max 2\nnew validated plan]
    REPLAN --> LOOP
    LOOP --> VERIFY{verified?}
    VERIFY -->|yes| REFLECT[REFLECTION → EXPERIENCE/MEMORY → RESPONSE completed]
    VERIFY -->|no, replans exhausted| FAIL2([FAILED\nsubsystem/operation/exception/recovery/result])
```

## Consciousness (runtime state, not sentience)

`LISTENING → UNDERSTANDING → THINKING → ACTIVE` (conversation) and
`UNDERSTANDING → PLANNING → EXECUTING → OBSERVING → VERIFYING →
REFLECTING → COMPLETED → ACTIVE` (tasks), with `ERROR → RECOVERING`
on genuine failures and `WAITING` while another attempt owns a task.
Transitions are validated; illegal jumps raise loudly.

## Stage 7: multi-step autonomy

- `decompose_goal()` splits explicit multi-action goals ("then", ";",
  newlines) into ordered steps; `build_capable_plan(..., chain=True)`
  links dependencies. Single-action goals are unchanged.
- Steps carry `step_id/goal/dependencies/required_capabilities/
  required_ability/inputs/expected_output/verification_criteria/risk`.
- The loop gates dependents on verified prerequisites (unmet deps block
  honestly), traces STEP/OBSERVATION/ABILITY/PERMISSION per step, and
  enforces MAX_REPLANS (2), MAX_STEP_RETRIES (1, authoritative over
  replan steps), MAX_TOTAL_EXECUTION_TIME (600s, per-run override).
- Replans classify failures (standard taxonomy), reuse experience
  preferences, and re-enter validation — never invent tools.
- Goals: queued → active → completed/failed/cancelled with priorities,
  dependencies, pause/resume. Tasks persist to `data/tasks.json`
  (`HERCULE_TASK_STORE` override, `:memory:` disables); resume skips
  verified steps, never replays them.
- Post-task self-evaluation (`goal_satisfied/steps_verified/replans/
  recovery/lesson`) is stored with the experience.
`Brain.health()` exposes state, focus, goal counts, recent
transitions — never chain-of-thought.

## Ability & tool layer

- `BaseAbility` is the developer interface: `name/description/capability/
  inputs/outputs/permissions/environments/verification/timeout_s/risk`
  plus `metadata()/validate_input()/environment_satisfied()`. New
  abilities subclass it — Brain is never modified.
- `AbilityManager.execute` validates capability → ability →
  permissions → environment → inputs, enforces HIGH-risk explicit
  approval (`approval_required=True` + `approved=True`), and logs
  `REQUEST → CAPABILITY → SELECTED ABILITY → PERMISSION → EXECUTION →
  VERIFICATION → RESULT`.
- `ToolMatcher.execute_with_fallback` treats structured failure dicts
  (`status` failed/error/pending) as fallback triggers across ranked
  candidates; only `status: success` reaches `verify_step`.
- `verify_math` recomputes calculator output independently; generic
  MATH content falls back to evidence-present.
- Real abilities: `calculator` + `mathematics` (AST arithmetic, MATH),
  `files` (sandboxed read/write/list, FILE_READ/FILE_WRITE),
  `diagnostics` (real OS/Python/CPU/memory, SYSTEM_OBSERVE),
  `terminal` (allowlisted read-only, no shell, 10s timeout,
  HIGH-risk approval, destructive patterns blocked).
- Planner never invents abilities: `validate_plan` + registry health +
  policy gate every step before execution.

## Honesty rules

- `UniversalFallbackMixin.__getattr__` raises honest `AttributeError`
  (subsystem/operation/recovery); it never synthesizes success.
- `OllamaAdapter`/`TransformersAdapter` implement real `generate()`.
- `ModelManager.generate` walks healthy adapters explicitly and
  returns structured `[HERCULE Error]` only after all fail.
- `AutonomousLoop` replans at most `max_replans` (default 2);
  verification (`verify_step`) decides success, never tool output alone.
- Semantic capability resolution is opt-in; deterministic inference
  is always the fallback.

## Benchmarks (this machine)

- `startup_ms≈130`, `think_hi_ms≈0.2`, `task_calculate_ms≈59`
  (`scripts/benchmark_lifecycle.py`).

# HERCULE-LM-100M Model Card — STATUS: NOT TRAINED (N6 BLOCKED)

This card describes the FROZEN CONFIGURATION, not a finished model.
No 100M checkpoint exists. Do not present this card as a trained
model release.

- Name: HERCULE-LM-100M (config v1, `hercule_lm_100m`).
- Architecture: causal decoder transformer (own NumPy code):
  vocab 16384, hidden 640, 16 layers, 10 heads, FFN 2560, ctx 512,
  learned positions, LayerNorm, GELU, Xavier init. 100,093,184 params.

# HERCULE-LM Backends: NumPy Reference + Torch (CPU/CUDA)

HERCULE-LM has two training backends for the **same architecture**
(token embedding + learned positions, N pre-norm transformer blocks
with causal multi-head attention and tanh-GELU FFN, final LayerNorm,
LM head, mean cross-entropy, Xavier-uniform random init, no
pretrained weights anywhere):

| Backend | Module | Device | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| NumPy reference | `models/hercule_lm/model.py` | CPU | correctness, deterministic tests, historical regression |
| Torch | `models/hercule_lm/torch_model.py` + `train_torch.py` | CPU and CUDA | real training, GPU execution |

QKV layout (both backends): one packed `qkvW [hidden, 3*hidden]`
reshaped to `[B,T,heads,3*head_dim]` and split per head into
`[Qh,Kh,Vh]`. Torch parameter names live under `blocks.<i>.<name>`
(`nn.Module` forbids `.` in registered names);
`numpy_param_dict()` / `load_numpy_param_dict()` translate to the
NumPy `L<i>.<name>` names. The architecture hash comes from the
shared `HerculeLMConfig`, so it is identical across backends.

## Selecting a backend

`python -m models.hercule_lm.train` (and `python -m training.run`,
which forwards `--device/--backend/--dtype/--amp`):

- `--device cpu` → NumPy reference (default).
- `--device cuda` / `cuda:N` → Torch on CUDA. Fails clearly
  (`DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, exit 2) when CUDA is missing. **Never falls
  back to CPU silently.**
- `--device auto` → Torch+CUDA when probed, else NumPy CPU.
- `--backend torch --device cpu` → Torch on CPU (parity/benchmark use).
- `--backend numpy --device cuda` → rejected (NumPy is CPU-only).

## CUDA requirements

- A CUDA-enabled PyTorch build (`torch.cuda.is_available() == True`)
  plus a visible GPU. This repo's dev box has a CPU-only torch, so
  CUDA paths are honest `NOT_RUN` skips here — see the report for how
  to validate on a GPU machine.
- FP32 first: compute is FP32 unless `--amp` is given.
- `--amp bf16` runs on CUDA (and CPU); `--amp fp16` requires CUDA
  (rejected clearly on CPU). AMP is recorded in the manifest; no
  speedup is claimed until measured.

## Exact commands

```bash
# NumPy CPU (reference)
python -m training.run --config models/hercule_lm/configs/hercule_lm_micro.json --device cpu --steps 10

# Torch CUDA (real GPU training)
python -m training.run --config models/hercule_lm/configs/hercule_lm_micro.json --device cuda --steps 10

# CUDA dry-run (gate only, no training)
python -m training.run --config models/hercule_lm/configs/hercule_lm_100m.json --device cuda --steps 10 --dry-run

# Direct trainer smoke (torch CPU on this box)
python -m models.hercule_lm.train --config hercule_lm_nano --backend torch --device cpu --steps 10

# Resume a torch run
python -m models.hercule_lm.train --config <cfg> --backend torch --device cuda \
  --resume training/checkpoints/<run>/step_<N> --steps <M>
```

`--steps N` is a **bounded benchmark**, not proof that full
pretraining is practical; full runs still go through the hardware
timeline-feasibility gate.

## Checkpoint formats

- NumPy: `weights.npz + manifest.json`,
  `checkpoint_format="hercule-npz-v1"`. Unchanged and loadable.
- Torch: `weights.pt` (model + optimizer + torch RNG) **plus**
  `weights.npz` (params-only export) + `manifest.json` with
  `checkpoint_format="hercule-torch-v1"`, `backend="torch"`,
  `device/dtype/amp`, architecture hash, tokenizer checksum, dataset
  hash, random-init origin.
- Resume validates architecture/tokenizer/dataset identity and
  rejects mismatches (`CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH`, `TOKENIZER_MISMATCH`,
  `DATASET_HASH_MISMATCH`).
- `map_to` is explicit: `cpu` always works; `cuda*` needs CUDA and a
  torch model (the NumPy model is CPU-only and fails clearly).
  Cross-backend resume (NumPy `.npz` → torch) is an explicit
  conversion with a fresh optimizer.

## CPU vs CUDA differences

- Initialization is bit-identical across backends for the same seed
  (same NumPy RNG draw order); CPU training trajectories reproduce
  under fixed seed+order (verified: resumed step-40 loss exactly
  equals the uninterrupted run).
- CUDA trajectories are **not** claimed bit-identical to CPU
  (parallel reduction order, cuDNN kernels). Parity tolerances:
  forward logits rtol=1e-4/atol=1e-5, loss abs<1e-4, grads
  rtol=1e-4/atol=1e-6, one AdamW step rtol=1e-2/**atol=1e-4**.
- The looser optimizer-step tolerance is principled: Adam divides by
  `|g|`, so coordinates whose true gradient cancels to ~0 take
  different tiny steps while agreeing in absolute terms (worst
  observed absolute drift after one lr=1e-3 step: ~4e-5, confined to
  near-zero updates).

## Deterministic guarantees and limitations

- Same seed + same backend + same device + same batch order →
  reproducible (torch seeded: `manual_seed`, `cuda.manual_seed_all`,
  cuDNN deterministic, NumPy/Python seeded).
- Across backends/devices: close within the tolerances above, never
  bit-identical — and never claimed so.
- Data pipeline (tokenizer, cached streams, manifests, splits,
  leakage/licensing checks) is shared, not rewritten; batches convert
  NumPy→torch once per micro-batch.

## Multi-GPU status

Single-device by default. DDP infrastructure is implemented
(`models/hercule_lm/distributed.py`, launcher `scripts/ddp_launch.py`):

```bash
# 2-GPU (on a 2-GPU box; NOT validated — 0 GPUs here)
python scripts/ddp_launch.py --nproc 2 -- \
  -m models.hercule_lm.train --config hercule_lm_nano \
  --backend torch --device cuda --steps 100
```

A 2-process CPU/gloo harness run passes (proves plumbing, gradient
sync, rank-0 checkpointing) but is **not** multi-GPU proof.
`distributed_status` reports `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` single-device,
`DDP <backend> world_size=N` in distributed runs. FSDP scaffold
(`models/hercule_lm/fsdp.py`) refuses single-process wrapping.
Multi-GPU is claimed only after a real ≥ 2-CUDA-device run.

# HERCULE-LM Kaggle GPU Training Pipeline

Local PC orchestrates; Kaggle GPU trains. Never the reverse.

## Setup (once)

1. `pip install kaggle` (already in `.venv`)
2. Kaggle Settings → Account → API → Create New Token, then either:
   - set `KAGGLE_USERNAME` + `KAGGLE_KEY` env vars, or
   - place `kaggle.json` at `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
3. Verify: `python -m tools.kaggle_trainer.controller latest`

## First target (gates A–I)

```bash
python -m tools.kaggle_trainer.controller new-run \
  --config hercule_lm_micro --steps 100 --mode benchmark --run-id smoke-01
python -m tools.kaggle_trainer.controller status --run-id smoke-01
python -m tools.kaggle_trainer.controller logs --run-id smoke-01 --lines 40
python -m tools.kaggle_trainer.controller download --run-id smoke-01
python -m tools.kaggle_trainer.controller evaluate --run-id smoke-01 \
  --tokenizer-dir <dir>
```

Gates A–I execute inside the remote job (`smoke.json`): GPU detected,
CUDA detected, Torch backend, forward/backward, optimizer step,
checkpoint save/load, 100-step benchmark, throughput recorded. Any
gate failure aborts with a `REMOTE_FAIL [CODE]` record — never a
silent CPU fallback.

## Continuous training

`--resume`, `--continue` (new run from downloaded checkpoint),
`--evaluate`, `--status`, `--logs`, `--cancel`, `--download`,
`--latest`. Programmatic: `train_remote(model, dataset, config,
steps, gpu, resume_from=None)` returns a structured result dict.

## Safety

- Bundles exclude `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.git`, secrets (filename +
  content scan; build refuses on hit).
- Downloaded checkpoints are registered, NEVER auto-approved.
  Adoption requires `checkpoints.adopt(run_id, reason, evidence)`.
- Failure classes: quota/accelerator/timeout retry (bounded);
  code/data/checkpoint never retried blindly.
- Execution labels: LOCAL_CPU / REMOTE_CPU(debug only) /
  REMOTE_CUDA / REMOTE_MULTI_GPU. A GPU claim requires measured
  remote telemetry.

pass tasks with zero model contribution — the random-control
comparison (untrained vs trained checkpoint on identical suites) is
the only accepted evidence of training effect.

suite record; framework-level 64-task runs with hercule-lm bound

## Stage R3 — ARC/Program-Search Reasoning

**Goal:** Improve compositional reasoning while preserving honest evaluation.

**Current Verified State (from `arc_reasoning/` + tests):**
- Relation-conditioned copy/place with 64 → 16 → 1 parsimony funnel
- Invariance checks: landmark_translation, canvas_padding, background_recolor (core); palette_rename reported only
- Selectors: shape, color, area, orientation, unique-color/shape/size, most/least-frequent-color
- Placements: onto_marker, align_bbox, adjacent, between, mirrored_across, repeated_k
- Candidate ranking: heavy local-rewrite penalty (10×/20×), relation predicate bonus
- 40 tests passing (39 ARC + 1 funnel test)
- Current benchmark: 7/128 tasks solved on discovery split (baseline v3)

**Requirements:**
- Preserve frozen task split discipline (never alter benchmark tasks to improve scores)
- Record: raw hypotheses → after parsimony funnel → invariance survivors → selected candidate
- Record intended-rule rank when known
- Record test-grid exact result
- Record timeout/search budget
- Separate generated, accepted, selected, and correct rules in reports

**Current Known Research Issue:**
Relation-conditioned-copy tasks can yield many exact-fit and invariant hypotheses. The current parsimony features (selector_bits + placement_rank) may not distinguish the intended `onto_marker` relation from competing `adjacent` or `align_bbox` variants.

**Next Priority (in order):**
1. **Counterfactual discrimination:** Insert distractors that break spurious `align_bbox`/`adjacent` matches but preserve `onto_marker`
2. **Independent landmark/source transformations:** Test that rule tracks landmark when source also moves
3. **Distractor insertion tests:** Extra objects that create false selector matches
4. **Cross-example role consistency:** Verify selector picks same role across all training pairs
5. **Whole-task compression/generalization signals:** Prefer rules that compress the task description

**Non-goals:**
- Adding large numbers of new primitives before showing existing tied candidates can be differentiated more reliably
- Claiming ARC-AGI-2 progress without frozen public evaluation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- New discriminator reduces 64→16 funnel to ≤8 candidates on marker-tracking tasks
- Correct `onto_marker` rule ranks #1 in ≥80% of marker-tracking tasks
- All 40 existing tests still pass
- Frozen discovery split score reported honestly

**Dependencies:** R0 experiment logging, R2 small experiment infrastructure

# HERCULE-LM-100M — Model Card (EXPERIMENTAL, untrained at this scale)

Version: config v1 (no 100M checkpoint exists — see limitations).

- Architecture: causal decoder transformer (HERCULE-authored NumPy):
  learned absolute positions, pre-norm LayerNorm blocks, causal MHA,
  GELU FFN, residual connections, output projection.
- Configuration (`models/hercule_lm/configs/hercule_lm_100m.json`):
  vocab 16384, hidden 640, 16 layers, 10 heads, FFN 2560, context 512,
  Xavier-uniform init, seed-controlled. **Parameter count: 100,093,184**
  (computed, matches implementation layout exactly).
- Tokenizer: own byte-level BPE (`hercule-bpe-100m-v1`, 16384).
- Training data: `hercule-seed-v1` (HERCULE-authored/synthetic, MIT).
- Initialization: random (Xavier-uniform); no pretrained weights anywhere.
- Hardware used: none at 100M scale (see below).
- Training duration: N/A — **pretraining BLOCKED, insufficient compute**
  (2-core CPU ≈ 10 tok/s projected at 100M; ~1B tokens ≈ 3 years).
- Proven smaller siblings: nano (0.93M, trained, ppl 14.4),
  micro (3.09M, trained 291 steps, valid loss 1.53 / ppl 4.6,
  random control ppl 1219.6).
- Limitations: 100M config defined/validated but never trained;
  small models learn answer shapes before arithmetic; NumPy CPU only.
- Intended use: research into from-scratch HERCULE models.
- Non-intended use: production reasoning, safety-critical decisions.
- Known failures: small checkpoints repeat frequent tokens; 0/30
  held-out arithmetic exact-match at micro scale.
- Checksum: config hash recorded per checkpoint manifest at train time.
