from __future__ import annotations
"""HERCULE-LM dataset pipeline (N3 §7/§8/§10/§16).

Documents are explicit files with per-source license metadata —
never production memory, never scraped content. Splits are by
document hash (deterministic, leakage-free). Validation refuses to
train on malformed, duplicate, unlicensed, or contaminated data.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

import numpy as np


@dataclass
class DataSource:
    name: str
    license: str
    origin: str                      # "hercule-authored" | "hercule-synthetic" | ...
    url: str = ""
    version: str = "v1"
    files: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class Document:
    doc_id: str
    source: str
    license: str
    text: str

    def doc_hash(self) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(
            f"{self.source}\x00{self.text}".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def load_documents(root: str, sources: Sequence[DataSource],
                   paragraphs: bool = False) -> List[Document]:
    docs: List[Document] = []
    for source in sources:
        for rel in source.files:
            path = Path(root) / rel
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            chunks = [c for c in text.split("\n\n") if c.strip()] if paragraphs else [text]
            for index, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
                doc_id = f"{source.name}:{Path(rel).name}#{index}" if paragraphs \
                    else f"{source.name}:{Path(rel).name}"
                docs.append(Document(doc_id, source.name, source.license, chunk.strip() + "\n"))
    return docs


def validate_documents(docs: Sequence[Document],
                       allowed_licenses: Sequence[str],
                       forbidden_hashes: Optional[Set[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Refuse-to-train gate. Returns a report; raises on critical failure."""
    problems: List[str] = []
    seen_text: Set[str] = set()
    seen_ids: Set[str] = set()
    for doc in docs:
        if not doc.text.strip():
            problems.append(f"EMPTY_DOCUMENT: {doc.doc_id}")
        if doc.doc_id in seen_ids:
            problems.append(f"DUPLICATE_ID: {doc.doc_id}")
        seen_ids.add(doc.doc_id)
        digest = hashlib.sha256(doc.text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        if digest in seen_text:
            problems.append(f"DUPLICATE_DOCUMENT: {doc.doc_id}")
        seen_text.add(digest)
        if doc.license not in allowed_licenses:
            problems.append(f"UNSUPPORTED_LICENSE: {doc.doc_id} ({doc.license})")
        if forbidden_hashes and doc.doc_hash() in forbidden_hashes:
            problems.append(f"CONTAMINATED: {doc.doc_id}")
        try:
            doc.text.encode("utf-8")
        except Exception:
            problems.append(f"IMPOSSIBLE_ENCODING: {doc.doc_id}")
    report = {"documents": len(docs), "problems": problems,
              "critical": [p for p in problems if p.split(':')[0] in
                           {"EMPTY_DOCUMENT", "UNSUPPORTED_LICENSE",
                            "CONTAMINATED", "IMPOSSIBLE_ENCODING"}]}
    if report["critical"]:
        raise ValueError("INVALID_DATASET: " + "; ".join(report["critical"][:5]))
    return report


def split_documents(docs: Sequence[Document], train: float = 0.9,
                    valid: float = 0.05) -> Dict[str, List[Document]]:
    """Deterministic hash split — no document crosses a boundary, ever."""
    buckets: Dict[str, List[Document]] = {"train": [], "validation": [], "test": []}
    for doc in docs:
        slot = int(doc.doc_hash()[:8], 16) % 1000 / 1000.0
        if slot < train:
            buckets["train"].append(doc)
        elif slot < train + valid:
            buckets["validation"].append(doc)
        else:
            buckets["test"].append(doc)
    return buckets


def check_no_leakage(splits: Dict[str, List[Document]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    sets = {k: {d.doc_hash() for d in v} for k, v in splits.items()}
    overlap = (sets["train"] & sets["validation"]) | \
              (sets["train"] & sets["test"]) | (sets["validation"] & sets["test"])
    return {"overlap": sorted(overlap),
            "sizes": {k: len(v) for k, v in splits.items()}}


def _shingles(text: str, k: int = 5) -> set:
    tokens = str(text or "").lower().split()
    if len(tokens) < k:
        return {tuple(tokens)} if tokens else set()
    return {tuple(tokens[i:i + k]) for i in range(len(tokens) - k + 1)}


def near_duplicates(docs: Sequence[Document], threshold: float = 0.8,
                    k: int = 5) -> List[List[str]]:
    """Near-duplicate groups via word-shingle Jaccard (deterministic).

    O(n^2) set ops — practical for thousand-scale corpora; reported,
    never auto-deleted.
    """
    sigs = [(d.doc_id, _shingles(d.text, k)) for d in docs]
    groups: List[List[str]] = []
    used: set = set()
    for i, (doc_id, sig) in enumerate(sigs):
        if doc_id in used or not sig:
            continue
        group = [doc_id]
        for j in range(i + 1, len(sigs)):
            other_id, other = sigs[j]
            if other_id in used or not other:
                continue
            union = len(sig | other)
            if union and len(sig & other) / union >= threshold:
                group.append(other_id)
                used.add(other_id)
        if len(group) > 1:
            used.add(doc_id)
            groups.append(sorted(group))
    return sorted(groups)


def quality_dimensions(docs: Sequence[Document]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Measurable quality dimensions (frontier P6): counts, not verdicts."""
    import re as _re

    texts = [d.text for d in docs]
    code_markers = ("def ", "return", "import ", "{", "}", ";", "==")
    math_markers = ("+", "-", "*", "/", "=", "Calculate")
    fact_cues = ("is ", "are ", "was ", "were ")
    instr_cues = ("USER:", "TARGET:", "?", "Plan:", "Classify")
    dims: Dict[str, Any] = {"documents": len(docs)}
    lengths = sorted(len(t) for t in texts) if texts else [0]
    toks = sorted(len(t.split()) for t in texts) if texts else [0]
    dims["doc_chars_p50"] = lengths[len(lengths) // 2]
    dims["doc_chars_max"] = lengths[-1]
    dims["doc_words_p50"] = toks[len(toks) // 2]
    dims["code_like"] = sum(1 for t in texts if any(m in t for m in code_markers))
    dims["math_like"] = sum(1 for t in texts if any(m in t for m in math_markers))
    dims["factual_like"] = sum(1 for t in texts if any(m in t for m in fact_cues))
    dims["instructional_like"] = sum(1 for t in texts if any(m in t for m in instr_cues))
    rep_ratio = 0.0
    if texts:
        rep_ratio = 1.0 - len(set(texts)) / len(texts)
    dims["repetition_ratio"] = round(rep_ratio, 3)
    langs = {"non_ascii": sum(1 for t in texts if any(ord(c) > 127 for c in t))}
    dims["language_distribution"] = {"ascii_only": len(texts) - langs["non_ascii"], **langs}
    return dims


def dataset_manifest(name: str, version: str, sources: Sequence[DataSource],
                     docs: Sequence[Document],
                     splits: Dict[str, List[Document]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    texts = sorted(d.doc_hash() for d in docs)
    digest = hashlib.sha256("".join(texts).encode()).hexdigest()
    return {
        "name": name, "version": version,
        "sources": [{"name": s.name, "license": s.license, "origin": s.origin,
                     "url": s.url, "version": s.version,
                     "files": list(s.files)} for s in sources],
        "documents": len(docs),
        "dataset_hash": digest,
        "splits": {k: {"documents": len(v),
                       "hash": hashlib.sha256(
                           "".join(sorted(d.doc_hash() for d in v)).encode()
                       ).hexdigest()[:16]} for k, v in splits.items()},
    }


def encode_split(tokenizer, docs: Sequence[Document], seq_len: int,
                 seed: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Concatenate encoded docs with EOS separators → token stream."""
    stream: List[int] = []
    for doc in docs:
        ids = tokenizer.encode(doc.text, add_eos=True)
        if ids:
            stream.extend(ids)
    return np.asarray(stream, dtype=np.int64)


CACHE_FORMAT = "hercule-stream-v1"


def cached_stream(tokenizer, docs: Sequence[Document], seq_len: int,
                  seed: int, cache_dir: str,
                  corpus_hash: str = "") -> np.ndarray:
    """Deterministic cached token stream (N4 §13): skips repeat BPE.

    Cache key covers corpus hash + tokenizer checksum + seq_len +
    format version; any change invalidates (falls back to encoding
    and rewrites). Byte-identical to ``encode_split`` on a hit.
    """
    from pathlib import Path as _Path
    import json as _json

    key = hashlib.sha256(
        f"{CACHE_FORMAT}\x00{corpus_hash}\x00{tokenizer.checksum()}\x00{seq_len}".encode()
    ).hexdigest()[:16]
    directory = _Path(cache_dir)
    manifest_path = directory / f"stream-{key}.manifest.json"
    stream_path = directory / f"stream-{key}.npy"
    if manifest_path.exists() and stream_path.exists():
        try:
            meta = _json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if meta.get("key") == key:
                return np.load(stream_path)
        except Exception:
            pass
    stream = encode_split(tokenizer, docs, seq_len, seed=seed)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # np.save appends .npy when missing, so the temp name must already
    # end in .npy for the atomic replace below to find it.
    tmp = directory / f"stream-{key}.tmp.npy"
    np.save(tmp, stream)
    tmp.replace(stream_path)
    manifest_path.write_text(_json.dumps(
        {"key": key, "format": CACHE_FORMAT, "corpus_hash": corpus_hash,
         "tokenizer_checksum": tokenizer.checksum(), "seq_len": seq_len,
         "tokens": int(stream.size)}), encoding="utf-8")
    return stream


def make_batches(stream: np.ndarray, seq_len: int, batch_size: int,
                 seed: int, pad_id: int = 0) -> List[Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]:
    """Sliding-window (input, shifted-target) batches, deterministic order."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    usable = (len(stream) - 1) // seq_len
    if usable < 1:
        raise ValueError("NO_DATASET: stream shorter than one sequence")
    order = rng.permutation(usable)
    batches = []
    for start in range(0, usable, batch_size):
        chunk = order[start:start + batch_size]
        xs = np.stack([stream[i * seq_len:(i + 1) * seq_len] for i in chunk])
        ys = np.stack([stream[i * seq_len + 1:(i + 1) * seq_len + 1] for i in chunk])
        batches.append((xs.astype(np.int64), ys.astype(np.int64)))
    return batches


def mask_before_marker(ids: np.ndarray, marker_ids: list,
                        ignore_id: int = -100) -> np.ndarray:
    """SFT label masking: positions up to and including the first
    occurrence of the marker span are ignored (instruction region);
    everything after trains. No marker → unmasked copy."""
    labels = np.asarray(ids).copy()
    if not marker_ids:
        return labels
    flat = labels.ravel()
    width = len(marker_ids)
    for start in range(len(flat) - width + 1):
        if [int(x) for x in flat[start:start + width]] == list(marker_ids):
            labels.ravel()[:start + width] = ignore_id
            return labels
    return labels


class ShardedStream:
    """Streaming loader over .npy token shards (frontier P7).

    Larger-than-RAM datasets stay on disk: one shard resident at a
    time, sequential deterministic order, resumable cursor
    ({shard, offset}) compatible with checkpoint state. Single-device
    rank 0 consumes all shards; other ranks report empty (multi-GPU
    sharding is PLANNED, not faked).
    """

    def __init__(self, shards: Sequence[str], rank: int = 0, world_size: int = 1):
        paths = [str(s) for s in shards]
        if rank == 0:
            self._paths = paths
        else:
            self._paths = []  # non-zero ranks: no fake data
        self.rank = rank
        self.world_size = world_size
        self.shard_index = 0
        self.offset = 0
        self._current: Optional[np.ndarray] = None

    def state_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {"shard_index": self.shard_index, "offset": self.offset,
                "rank": self.rank, "world_size": self.world_size,
                "shards": list(self._paths)}

    def load_state_dict(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        if list(state.get("shards", [])) != list(self._paths):
            raise ValueError("STREAM_MISMATCH: shard list changed")
        self.shard_index = int(state.get("shard_index", 0))
        self.offset = int(state.get("offset", 0))
        self._current = None

    def _load_shard(self) -> bool:
        while self.shard_index < len(self._paths):
            try:
                self._current = np.load(self._paths[self.shard_index], mmap_mode="r")
                return True
            except Exception:
                self.shard_index += 1
                self.offset = 0
        self._current = None
        return False

    def next_batch(self, batch_size: int, seq_len: int) -> Optional[Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]:
        """Next sequential (inputs, shifted-targets) windows, or None at end."""
        need = batch_size * seq_len + 1
        buf = np.zeros(need, dtype=np.int64)
        filled = 0
        while filled < need:
            if self._current is None and not self._load_shard():
                return None
            assert self._current is not None
            available = len(self._current) - self.offset
            if available <= 0:
                self._current = None
                self.shard_index += 1
                self.offset = 0
                continue
            take = min(available, need - filled)
            buf[filled:filled + take] = self._current[self.offset:self.offset + take]
            filled += take
            self.offset += take
        xs = buf[:batch_size * seq_len].reshape(batch_size, seq_len)
        ys = buf[1:batch_size * seq_len + 1].reshape(batch_size, seq_len)
        return xs, ys

from __future__ import annotations
"""Next-generation dataset pipeline (Phase 4H): auditable, deterministic.

Builds on :mod:`models.hercule_lm.data` (sources, validation, splits,
manifests, shingle near-dup, quality dimensions, sharded streams) by
adding the pieces Phase 4 requires:

- language identification (heuristic, script-based; labeled as such)
- per-document quality scoring (documented formula, deterministic)
- exact dedup (keeps first occurrence, reports removals)
- near-dedup filtering (reuses shingle-Jaccard groups)
- contamination scan against probe texts (explicit probe list)
- declarative filtering (length / repetition / language / license)
- shard writer (.npy token shards + manifest, resumable-cursor ready)
- one orchestrator: ``build_dataset`` -> (docs, splits, manifest, report)

No network, no external models, no pretrained anything. Every
heuristic is documented in the report it produces; sampling (used only
for O(n^2) near-dup on large corpora) is recorded, never hidden.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

from .data import (DataSource, Document, check_no_leakage, dataset_manifest,
                   near_duplicates, quality_dimensions, split_documents,
                   validate_documents)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- language

_BENGALI = ("bengali", 0x0980, 0x09FF)
_DEVANAGARI = ("hindi", 0x0900, 0x097F)  # Hindi in Devanagari script
_LATIN = ("latin", 0x0041, 0x007A)


def guess_language(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Heuristic script-based language guess (NOT a trained identifier).

    Counts characters in the Bengali, Devanagari, and Latin ranges plus
    CJK/other; returns the majority script mapped to a language label.
    Mixed content reports ``mixed`` with fractions. Deterministic.
    """
    counts = {"bengali": 0, "hindi": 0, "english": 0, "other": 0}
    total = 0
    for ch in text:
        o = ord(ch)
        if ch.isspace():
            continue
        total += 1
        if 0x0980 <= o <= 0x09FF:
            counts["bengali"] += 1
        elif 0x0900 <= o <= 0x097F:
            counts["hindi"] += 1
        elif ch.isascii() and ch.isalpha():
            counts["english"] += 1
        else:
            counts["other"] += 1
    if total == 0:
        return {"language": "unknown", "fractions": {}, "method": "script-heuristic"}
    fracs = {k: round(v / total, 3) for k, v in counts.items()}
    best = max(counts, key=lambda k: counts[k])
    label = best if fracs[best] >= 0.5 else "mixed"
    return {"language": label, "fractions": fracs, "method": "script-heuristic"}


def language_distribution(docs: Sequence[Document]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    dist: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for doc in docs:
        lang = guess_language(doc.text)["language"]
        dist[lang] = dist.get(lang, 0) + 1
    return {"documents": len(docs), "by_language": dist,
            "method": "script-heuristic (see guess_language)"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- quality

def quality_score(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Deterministic per-document quality score in [0, 1].

    Formula (documented, heuristic):
      base 0.5
      +0.2 if 50 <= chars <= 20000 (reasonable length)
      +0.1 if 10 <= words <= 4000
      +0.1 if repetition (dup lines / total lines) < 0.3
      +0.05 for code markers, +0.05 for math markers (content signal)
      -0.3 if > 50% non-alphanumeric noise
    Scores are signals for filtering, never verdicts about truth.
    """
    import re as _re

    chars = len(text)
    words = len(text.split())
    lines = [ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    rep = 0.0
    if lines:
        rep = 1.0 - len(set(lines)) / len(lines)
    alnum = sum(1 for c in text if c.isalnum() or c.isspace())
    noise = 1.0 - (alnum / max(1, len(text)))
    score = 0.5
    if 50 <= chars <= 20000:
        score += 0.2
    if 10 <= words <= 4000:
        score += 0.1
    if rep < 0.3:
        score += 0.1
    code_markers = ("def ", "return", "import ", "{", "}", ";", "==")
    math_markers = ("+", "-", "*", "/", "=", "Calculate")
    if any(m in text for m in code_markers):
        score += 0.05
    if any(m in text for m in math_markers):
        score += 0.05
    if noise > 0.5:
        score -= 0.3
    score = max(0.0, min(1.0, round(score, 3)))
    return {"score": score, "chars": chars, "words": words,
            "line_repetition": round(rep, 3), "noise_ratio": round(noise, 3)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dedup

def dedup_exact(docs: Sequence[Document]) -> Tuple[List[Document], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Drop byte-exact duplicate texts (keep first). Deterministic."""
    seen: Set[str] = set()
    kept: List[Document] = []
    removed = 0
    for doc in docs:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(doc.text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        if digest in seen:
            removed += 1
            continue
        seen.add(digest)
        kept.append(doc)
    return kept, {"input": len(docs), "kept": len(kept), "removed_exact": removed}


def filter_near_duplicates(docs: Sequence[Document], threshold: float = 0.8,
                           k: int = 5, cap: int = 2000) -> Tuple[List[Document], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Drop near-duplicates (keep first per group). Deterministic.

    ``cap`` bounds the O(n^2) scan: groups are computed on the first
    ``cap`` documents; beyond that the scan is SKIPPED and reported
    (never silently partial).
    """
    if len(docs) > cap:
        return list(docs), {"input": len(docs), "kept": len(docs),
                            "removed_near": 0, "skipped": True,
                            "reason": f"corpus ({len(docs)}) exceeds cap ({cap}); "
                                      "run sharded offline for full near-dedup"}
    groups = near_duplicates(docs, threshold=threshold, k=k)
    drop_ids: Set[str] = set()
    for group in groups:
        for doc_id in sorted(group)[1:]:
            drop_ids.add(doc_id)
    kept = [d for d in docs if d.doc_id not in drop_ids]
    return kept, {"input": len(docs), "kept": len(kept),
                  "removed_near": len(drop_ids), "groups": len(groups),
                  "threshold": threshold, "k": k, "skipped": False}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- contamination

EVAL_PROBES = [
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    "Calculate 317 + 542.",
    "USER: Plan the route.\nTARGET:",
]


def contamination_scan(docs: Sequence[Document],
                       probes: Sequence[str] = (),
                       k: int = 5, threshold: float = 0.8) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Shingle-overlap scan of docs against explicit probe texts.

    Reports docs whose word-shingle Jaccard with ANY probe meets the
    threshold. The probe list is part of the report: this checks the
    listed probes only, never "all benchmarks".
    """
    from .data import _shingles

    probes = list(probes) or list(EVAL_PROBES)
    probe_sigs = [_shingles(p, k) for p in probes]
    hits: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for doc in docs:
        sig = _shingles(doc.text, k)
        if not sig:
            continue
        for i, psig in enumerate(probe_sigs):
            if not psig:
                continue
            union = len(sig | psig)
            jac = len(sig & psig) / union if union else 0.0
            if jac >= threshold:
                hits.append({"doc_id": doc.doc_id, "probe": i,
                             "jaccard": round(jac, 3)})
                break
    return {"probes": len(probes), "documents": len(docs),
            "hits": hits, "hit_count": len(hits), "k": k,
            "threshold": threshold,
            "note": "probe-list scan only; extend probes for wider coverage"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- filtering

def filter_documents(docs: Sequence[Document],
                     min_chars: int = 20, max_chars: int = 50000,
                     max_rep: float = 0.7, min_score: float = 0.0,
                     allowed_languages: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
                     allowed_licenses: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> Tuple[List[Document], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Declarative filter; every rejection reason is counted."""
    reasons: Dict[str, int] = {}
    kept: List[Document] = []

    def reject(doc: Document, why: str) -> None:
        reasons[why] = reasons.get(why, 0) + 1

    for doc in docs:
        if allowed_licenses is not None and doc.license not in allowed_licenses:
            reject(doc, "license")
            continue
        if not (min_chars <= len(doc.text) <= max_chars):
            reject(doc, "length")
            continue
        info = quality_score(doc.text)
        if info["score"] < min_score or info["line_repetition"] > max_rep:
            reject(doc, "quality")
            continue
        if allowed_languages is not None:
            lang = guess_language(doc.text)["language"]
            if lang not in allowed_languages and "mixed" not in allowed_languages:
                reject(doc, f"language:{lang}")
                continue
        kept.append(doc)
    return kept, {"input": len(docs), "kept": len(kept), "rejected": reasons,
                  "params": {"min_chars": min_chars, "max_chars": max_chars,
                             "max_rep": max_rep, "min_score": min_score,
                             "allowed_languages": list(allowed_languages or []),
                             "allowed_licenses": list(allowed_licenses or [])}}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sharding

SHARD_FORMAT = "hercule-shard-v1"


def write_shards(stream, seq_len: int, shard_tokens: int, out_dir: str,
                 prefix: str = "shard") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Write a token stream as fixed-size .npy shards + manifest.

    Shard ``i`` holds stream[i*N:(i+1)*N]. Manifest records hashes for
    integrity; ``ShardedStream`` consumes the shards with a resumable
    cursor.
    """
    import numpy as np

    arr = np.asarray(stream, dtype=np.int64)
    total = int(arr.size)
    target = Path(out_dir)
    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shards = []
    for i, start in enumerate(range(0, total, shard_tokens)):
        path = target / f"{prefix}-{i:05d}.npy"
        chunk = np.ascontiguousarray(arr[start:start + shard_tokens])
        tmp = target / f"{prefix}-{i:05d}.tmp.npy"
        np.save(tmp, chunk)
        tmp.replace(path)
        digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        shards.append({"path": str(path), "tokens": int(chunk.size),
                       "sha256": digest})
    manifest = {"format": SHARD_FORMAT, "seq_len": int(seq_len),
                "total_tokens": total, "shard_tokens": int(shard_tokens),
                "shards": shards}
    (target / "shards.manifest.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return manifest


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- orchestrator

def build_dataset(name: str, version: str, sources: Sequence[DataSource],
                  docs: Sequence[Document],
                  allowed_licenses: Sequence[str],
                  min_score: float = 0.0,
                  near_dup_threshold: float = 0.8,
                  probes: Sequence[str] = (),
                  forbidden_hashes: Optional[Set[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Full auditable pass: validate -> filter -> dedup -> splits -> manifest.

    Returns {"docs", "splits", "manifest", "leak", "report"} where report
    records every stage's counts and parameters.
    """
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"name": name, "version": version,
                              "input_documents": len(docs)}
    validate_documents(docs, allowed_licenses, forbidden_hashes)
    kept, freq = filter_documents(docs, min_score=min_score,
                                  allowed_licenses=list(allowed_licenses))
    report["filter"] = freq
    kept, exact = dedup_exact(kept)
    report["dedup_exact"] = exact
    kept, near = filter_near_duplicates(kept, threshold=near_dup_threshold)
    report["dedup_near"] = near
    report["languages"] = language_distribution(kept)
    report["quality"] = quality_dimensions(kept)
    scores = [quality_score(d.text)["score"] for d in kept]
    report["score_hist"] = {
        "n": len(scores),
        "mean": round(sum(scores) / max(1, len(scores)), 3),
        "lt_0_5": sum(1 for s in scores if s < 0.5),
        "ge_0_8": sum(1 for s in scores if s >= 0.8),
    }
    report["contamination"] = contamination_scan(kept, probes)
    splits = split_documents(kept)
    leak = check_no_leakage(splits)
    if leak["overlap"]:
        raise ValueError(f"DATASET LEAKAGE: {leak['overlap'][:3]}")
    report["splits"] = leak["sizes"]
    manifest = dataset_manifest(name, version, sources, kept, splits)
    report["dataset_hash"] = manifest["dataset_hash"]
    return {"docs": kept, "splits": splits, "manifest": manifest,
            "leak": leak, "report": report}

from __future__ import annotations
"""Device abstraction (N5 §3-§5): explicit, honest, CPU-first.

Backends: ``numpy`` (reference; always available) and ``torch``
(optional; used only when importable AND CUDA is requested and
present). No torch installation is attempted. A requested CUDA
device that is unavailable fails clearly — never silent CPU
fallback. CUDA multi-GPU: single-device only; distributed status
is PLANNED (see ``topology()``).
"""

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional


@dataclass
class DeviceInfo:
    backend: str          # numpy | torch
    device: str           # cpu | cuda | cuda:N
    available: bool
    name: str = ""
    count: int = 0
    memory_bytes: int = 0  # 0 = UNKNOWN, never invented
    dtype_support: tuple = ("float32",)

    def as_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {"backend": self.backend, "device": self.device,
                "available": self.available, "name": self.name,
                "count": self.count,
                "memory_bytes": self.memory_bytes or "UNKNOWN",
                "dtype_support": list(self.dtype_support)}


def _torch_info() -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    try:
        import torch
    except Exception:
        return None
    try:
        cuda = bool(torch.cuda.is_available())
    except Exception:
        cuda = False
    return {"torch_version": getattr(torch, "__version__", "?"), "cuda": cuda}


def describe_backend() -> DeviceInfo:
    """Actually detected backend (never claimed, always probed)."""
    info = _torch_info()
    if info is not None and info["cuda"]:
        import torch

        index = 0
        try:
            name = torch.cuda.get_device_name(index)
        except Exception:
            name = "CUDA device"
        try:
            total = int(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(index).total_memory)
        except Exception:
            total = 0
        return DeviceInfo(backend="torch", device="cuda", available=True,
                          name=name, count=int(torch.cuda.device_count()),
                          memory_bytes=total,
                          dtype_support=("float32", "float16", "bfloat16"))
    return DeviceInfo(backend="numpy", device="cpu", available=True,
                      name="CPU (NumPy reference backend)",
                      count=int(os.cpu_count() or 0),
                      dtype_support=("float32",))


def get_training_device(requested: str = "auto",
                        env_var: str = "HERCULE_LM_DEVICE") -> DeviceInfo:
    """Resolve an explicit device request.

    ``auto`` → best available (CUDA when probed, else CPU).
    ``cpu`` → NumPy CPU path, always available.
    ``cuda``/``cuda:N`` → torch+CUDA probed; raises when unavailable.
    Environment override wins when set and non-empty.
    """
    env = str(os.environ.get(env_var, "") or "").strip().lower()
    want = (env or str(requested or "auto")).strip().lower()
    if want in ("", "auto"):
        return describe_backend()
    if want == "cpu":
        base = describe_backend()
        return DeviceInfo(backend="numpy", device="cpu", available=True,
                          name=base.name if base.backend == "numpy" else "CPU (NumPy reference backend)",
                          count=int(os.cpu_count() or 0),
                          dtype_support=("float32",))
    if want == "cuda" or want.startswith("cuda:"):
        info = _torch_info()
        if info is None:
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but PyTorch is not installed "
                               "(HERCULE_LM_DEVICE=cuda unavailable; use cpu)")
        if not info["cuda"]:
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but torch.cuda.is_available() "
                               "is false (use cpu)")
        full = describe_backend()
        if want.startswith("cuda:"):
            try:
                index = int(want.split(":", 1)[1])
            except ValueError:
                raise RuntimeError(f"invalid device request: {requested!r}")
            if index >= full.count:
                raise RuntimeError(f"cuda:{index} out of range (count={full.count})")
            full.device = f"cuda:{index}"
        return full
    raise RuntimeError(f"invalid device request: {requested!r} "
                       "(expected auto|cpu|cuda|cuda:N)")


def move_batch_to_device(batch, device: DeviceInfo):
    """NumPy backend: batches are already host arrays (explicit no-op).

    The torch backend (when present) would transfer here. Returning
    the batch unchanged on CPU is correct placement, not a silent
    fallback — CUDA requests never reach this path unfulfilled.
    """
    return batch


def gpu_utilization(device_index: int = 0) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Sample GPU utilization via nvidia-smi (None when unavailable).

    Never fabricated: returns None when nvidia-smi is missing, the
    GPU is absent, or parsing fails. Fields are raw measurements.
    """
    import subprocess

    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["nvidia-smi",
             f"--id={int(device_index)}",
             "--query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu,power.draw",
             "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
        if out.returncode != 0:
            return None
        parts = [p.strip() for p in str(out.stdout or "").split(",")]
        if len(parts) < 5:
            return None

        def _num(text: str) -> Optional[float]:
            try:
                return float(text)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None

        return {"gpu_util_percent": _num(parts[0]),
                "mem_used_mb": _num(parts[1]),
                "mem_total_mb": _num(parts[2]),
                "temperature_c": _num(parts[3]),
                "power_w": _num(parts[4]),
                "source": "nvidia-smi"}
    except Exception:
        return None


def topology() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Single/multi-device posture (honest, no fake distribution)."""
    info = _torch_info()
    cuda = bool(info and info["cuda"])
    return {"world_size": 1, "rank": 0, "local_rank": 0,
            "device_count": describe_backend().count,
            "cuda_available": cuda,
            "distributed": "PLANNED (single-device only; no fake multi-GPU execution)"}


def collect_runtime(device: str = "cpu", dtype: str = "float32",
                    amp: str = "off", backend: str = "") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Machine-readable execution record (never fabricated).

    Reports the actually-probed backend/device, GPU identity, and real
    CUDA memory counters (0 when CUDA is absent — never invented).
    ``distributed_status`` is NOT_IMPLEMENTED until genuine
    multi-GPU training lands; a second visible GPU is not claimed.
    """
    info = _torch_info()
    cuda = bool(info and info["cuda"])
    record: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "backend": backend or ("torch" if cuda and str(device).startswith("cuda") else "numpy"),
        "device": str(device),
        "dtype": str(dtype),
        "amp": str(amp),
        "torch_version": (info or {}).get("torch_version", "not-installed"),
        "cuda_available": cuda,
        "gpu_name": "none",
        "gpu_count": 0,
        "allocated_memory_bytes": 0,
        "reserved_memory_bytes": 0,
        "peak_allocated_memory_bytes": 0,
        "peak_reserved_memory_bytes": 0,
        "distributed_status": "NOT_IMPLEMENTED (single-device only; "
                              "two visible GPUs are NOT claimed as 2-GPU training)",
    }
    if not cuda:
        return record
    try:
        import torch

        record["gpu_count"] = int(torch.cuda.device_count())
        try:
            record["gpu_name"] = torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)
        except Exception:
            record["gpu_name"] = "CUDA device"
        if str(device).startswith("cuda"):
            try:
                record["allocated_memory_bytes"] = int(torch.cuda.memory_allocated(device))
                record["reserved_memory_bytes"] = int(torch.cuda.memory_reserved(device))
                record["peak_allocated_memory_bytes"] = int(
                    torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(device))
                record["peak_reserved_memory_bytes"] = int(
                    torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved(device))
            except Exception:
                pass
    except Exception:
        pass
    return record

from __future__ import annotations
"""Resource estimators (N5 §19/§20): labeled ESTIMATES, never measurements.

Memory separates weights / gradients / optimizer / activations /
checkpoint. Time derives from a measured tokens/sec figure supplied
by the caller (see training/benchmark.py). Uncertainty is explicit.
"""

import math
from typing import Any, Dict


def estimate_memory(parameter_count: int, batch: int, seq_len: int,
                    hidden: int, layers: int, heads: int, vocab: int,
                    dtype_bytes: int = 4, optimizer: str = "adamw") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """ESTIMATE (MB) for fp32 AdamW training. Activations scale with B*T."""
    params = int(parameter_count)
    weights = params * dtype_bytes
    grads = params * dtype_bytes
    opt_mult = 2.0 if optimizer.lower() == "adamw" else 1.0
    opt_state = params * dtype_bytes * opt_mult
    # Activations (rough, fp32): embeddings + per-layer norms/attn/FFN
    # plus attention score matrices (B*H*T*T).
    per_tok = hidden * (8 + 4 * layers) + heads * seq_len
    activations = batch * seq_len * per_tok * dtype_bytes
    total = weights + grads + opt_state + activations
    return {
        "kind": "ESTIMATE",
        "model_memory_mb": round(weights / 1e6, 1),
        "gradient_memory_mb": round(grads / 1e6, 1),
        "optimizer_memory_mb": round(opt_state / 1e6, 1),
        "activation_memory_mb": round(activations / 1e6, 1),
        "checkpoint_memory_mb": round((weights + opt_state) / 1e6, 1),
        "total_training_mb": round(total / 1e6, 1),
        "assumptions": [f"dtype={dtype_bytes}B", f"optimizer={optimizer}",
                        "activations fully materialized (no checkpointing)",
                        "excludes Python/BLAS/framework overhead"],
    }


def estimate_time(tokens_per_sec: float, target_tokens: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """ESTIMATE wall time from a MEASURED throughput figure."""
    if tokens_per_sec <= 0 or target_tokens <= 0:
        raise ValueError("tokens_per_sec and target_tokens must be positive")
    seconds = target_tokens / float(tokens_per_sec)
    out = {"kind": "ESTIMATE", "seconds": round(seconds, 1),
           "hours": round(seconds / 3600, 2),
           "days": round(seconds / 86400, 2),
           "years": round(seconds / 31536000, 3),
           "uncertainty": ["excludes validation/checkpointing/startup",
                           "excludes interruptions and thermal throttling",
                           "assumes sustained measured throughput"]}
    return out


def format_duration(seconds: float) -> str:
    if seconds < 90:
        return f"{seconds:.0f}s"
    if seconds < 5400:
        return f"{seconds / 60:.1f}min"
    if seconds < 86400 * 3:
        return f"{seconds / 3600:.1f}h"
    if seconds < 31536000 * 2:
        return f"{seconds / 86400:.1f}d"
    return f"{seconds / 31536000:.2f}y"


def memory_for_config(config, batch: int, seq_len: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return estimate_memory(config.parameter_count(), batch, seq_len,
                           config.hidden_size, config.num_layers,
                           config.num_heads, config.vocab_size)

from __future__ import annotations
"""HERCULE-LM checkpoint evaluation CLI (N3 §20, levels 1-2).

Usage::

    python -m models.hercule_lm.evaluate --checkpoint <dir> [--arithmetic-n 50]

Level 1 (training health): validation loss + perplexity on the corpus
validation split. Level 2 (language): held-out 3-digit arithmetic
exact-match + generation samples. No HERCULE pipeline here — that is
N3 §20 level 3/4, run separately through the evaluation framework.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from . import checkpoint as ckpt
from .config import HerculeLMConfig
from .data import DataSource, encode_split, load_documents, split_documents
from .model import HerculeLM
from .tokenizer import HerculeBPETokenizer


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="hercule-lm-evaluate")
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tokenizer-dir", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--corpus-dir", default="training/data/raw")
    parser.add_argument("--sources", default="training/data/sources.json")
    parser.add_argument("--arithmetic-n", type=int, default=50)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        manifest = json.loads((Path(args.checkpoint) / "manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        config = HerculeLMConfig.from_dict(manifest["architecture"])
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"CHECKPOINT_CORRUPTED: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    tok_dir = args.tokenizer_dir or f"training/tokenizer/{config.tokenizer_id}"
    tokenizer = HerculeBPETokenizer.load(tok_dir)
    model = HerculeLM(config, seed=0)
    try:
        ckpt.load_checkpoint(args.checkpoint, model, strict=True)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    # ---- Level 1: validation health ----
    sources = [DataSource(**s) for s in json.loads(Path(args.sources).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    docs = load_documents(args.corpus_dir, sources, paragraphs=True)
    splits = split_documents(docs)
    seq_len = config.context_length // 2
    stream = encode_split(tokenizer, splits["validation"] or splits["train"], seq_len, seed=args.seed)
    losses: list = []
    accs: list = []
    try:
        from .data import make_batches
        batches = make_batches(stream, seq_len, 4, seed=args.seed)
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"NO_DATASET: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    for xs, ys in batches[:8]:
        logits, cache = model.forward(xs)
        loss, _ = model.loss_and_backward(logits, cache, ys)
        losses.append(loss)
        pred = logits.argmax(axis=-1)
        mask = ys != -100
        accs.append(float(((pred == ys) & mask).sum() / max(1, int(mask.sum()))))
    val_loss = float(sum(losses) / len(losses))
    result = {"checkpoint": args.checkpoint,
              "evaluation": "hercule-lm-eval-v1",
              "level1": {"valid_loss": round(val_loss, 4),
                         "perplexity": round(float(np.exp(min(20.0, val_loss))), 2),
                         "next_token_accuracy": round(float(sum(accs) / len(accs)), 4)}}

    # ---- Level 2: held-out arithmetic (3-digit, never in corpus pairs) ----
    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed + 1)
    exact, total = 0, 0
    samples = []
    for _ in range(args.arithmetic_n):
        a, b = int(rng.integers(100, 1000)), int(rng.integers(100, 1000))
        prompt = f"Q: Calculate {a} + {b}.\nA:"
        ids = model.generate(tokenizer.encode(prompt), max_new_tokens=10, temperature=0.0)
        text = tokenizer.decode(ids)
        continuation = text[len(prompt):].strip()
        # Extract the first token/number from the continuation
        # The expected format is "ANSWER." where ANSWER is the sum
        # Use exact match for the full expected answer (including period)
        want = str(a + b) + "."
        # Clean the continuation: take first token/number
        cont = continuation.strip().split()[0] if continuation.strip() else ""
        hit = (cont == want)
        exact += int(hit)
        total += 1
        if len(samples) < 5:
            samples.append({"prompt": prompt, "want": want, "got": continuation[:20], "hit": hit})
    result["level2"] = {"arithmetic_exact": exact, "arithmetic_total": total,
                        "rate": round(exact / max(1, total), 3), "samples": samples}
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=1))
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

from __future__ import annotations
"""FSDP / sharded-training scaffolding for HERCULE-LM (Phase 2I/3H).

Real ``torch.distributed.fsdp`` wrapping — no reimplementation of
sharding. Until DDP single-GPU correctness is green AND multi-GPU
hardware exists, this module reports NOT_IMPLEMENTED/NOT_RUN and its
wrapping entry point refuses to pretend.

 transformer auto-wrap policy targets the per-block modules
(``models.hercule_lm.torch_model._TorchBlock``) so each transformer
block becomes one sharded unit; embeddings/head stay replicated.
"""

from typing import Any, Dict


def fsdp_available() -> bool:
    try:
        import torch.distributed.fsdp  # noqa: F401

        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def fsdp_status() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Honest FSDP capability report."""
    from .distributed import ddp_status

    dist = ddp_status()
    if dist["cuda_device_count"] >= 2 and fsdp_available():
        state = "READY (hardware present, no FSDP run yet)"
    elif not fsdp_available():
        state = "NOT_IMPLEMENTED (torch.distributed.fsdp unavailable)"
    else:
        state = "NOT_IMPLEMENTED (requires >= 2 CUDA devices + proven DDP)"
    return {"fsdp_available": fsdp_available(),
            "cuda_device_count": dist["cuda_device_count"],
            "distributed_status": dist["distributed_status"],
            "fsdp_status": state}


def block_wrap_policy():
    """Auto-wrap policy: one FSDP unit per transformer block."""
    try:
        from torch.distributed.fsdp.wrap import transformer_auto_wrap_policy

        from .torch_model import _TorchBlock

        return transformer_auto_wrap_policy(
            transformer_layer_cls={_TorchBlock})
    except Exception as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"FSDP_UNAVAILABLE: cannot build wrap policy ({exc})")


def wrap_fsdp(model, device=None, offload_cpu: bool = False):
    """Wrap a torch model with fully-sharded data parallel.

    Requires an initialized multi-rank process group; refuses
    single-process wrapping (that would be fake sharding).
    """
    from .distributed import get_world_size, is_dist_initialized

    if not fsdp_available():
        raise RuntimeError("FSDP_UNAVAILABLE: torch.distributed.fsdp not importable")
    if not is_dist_initialized() or get_world_size() < 2:
        raise RuntimeError("FSDP_UNAVAILABLE: FSDP requires an initialized process "
                           "group with world_size >= 2 (single-process wrapping "
                           "would be fake sharding)")
    from torch.distributed.fsdp import CPUOffload, FullyShardedDataParallel as FSDP
    from torch.distributed.fsdp import MixedPrecision

    return FSDP(
        model,
        auto_wrap_policy=block_wrap_policy(),
        cpu_offload=CPUOffload(offload_params=bool(offload_cpu)),
        mixed_precision=None,  # FP32 first; AMP only via explicit --amp runs
        device_id=device,
    )

class GeneralizationTestCase:

    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    structured: bool = False


@dataclass
class GeneralizationResult:
    """Result of generalization evaluation."""
    test_case: GeneralizationTestCase
    model_output: str
    parsed_reasoning: Optional[StructuredReasoning]
    exact_match: bool
    partial_match: bool
    structured_valid: bool
    verification_passed: bool
    latency_ms: float

def generate_unseen_numbers(seed: int, count: int = 100, 
                            train_range: Tuple[int, int] = (1, 1000)) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate arithmetic with numbers outside training range."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cases = []
    
    # Test ranges: negative, very large, decimals (if supported)
    test_ranges = [
        (-10000, -1001),      # negative
        (1001, 10000),        # larger than train
        (100000, 1000000),    # much larger
    ]
    
    for i in range(count):
        range_idx = i % len(test_ranges)
        low, high = test_ranges[range_idx]
        a, b = rng.integers(low, high, 2)
        op = rng.choice(['+', '-', '*'])
        
        if op == '+':
            ans = a + b
        elif op == '-':
            ans = a - b
        else:
            ans = a * b
        
        cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(
            problem=f"Q: Calculate {a} {op} {b}.\nA:",
            target=str(ans),
            domain="arithmetic",
            difficulty=2,
            generalization_type="unseen_numbers",
            metadata={"a": int(a), "b": int(b), "operator": op, "range": f"[{low},{high}]"}
        ))
    
    return cases


def generate_unseen_grid_properties(seed: int, count: int = 50) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate ARC grids with unseen colors, sizes, positions."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cases = []
    
    transforms = [
        ("invert", lambda g: [[1-v for v in row] for row in g]),
        ("rot90", lambda g: list(zip(*g[::-1]))),
        ("rot180", lambda g: [row[::-1] for row in g[::-1]]),
        ("flip_h", lambda g: [row[::-1] for row in g]),
        ("flip_v", lambda g: g[::-1]),
        ("transpose", lambda g: list(zip(*g))),
    ]
    
    for i in range(count):
        # Unseen grid sizes (larger than training 3-5)
        h = rng.integers(6, 10)
        w = rng.integers(6, 10)
        
        # Unseen colors (training: 0-4, test: 5-9)
        grid = [[rng.integers(5, 10) for _ in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]
        
        name, fn = rng.choice(transforms)
        try:
            result = fn(grid)
            result = [list(row) for row in result]
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        grid_str = ' '.join(''.join(str(v) for v in row) for row in grid)
        result_str = ' '.join(''.join(str(v) for v in row) for row in result)
        
        cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(
            problem=f"Q: Transform grid: {grid_str}\nA:",
            target=result_str,
            domain="arc_grid",
            difficulty=3,
            generalization_type="unseen_grid_properties",
            metadata={"transform": name, "grid_size": f"{h}x{w}", "colors": "5-9"}
        ))
    
    return cases


def generate_compositional_generalization(seed: int, count: int = 50) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate compositional tasks (combine known transforms)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cases = []
    
    # Training has single transforms; test has compositions
    transforms = [
        ("invert", lambda g: [[1-v for v in row] for row in g]),
        ("rot90", lambda g: list(zip(*g[::-1]))),
        ("rot180", lambda g: [row[::-1] for row in g[::-1]]),
        ("flip_h", lambda g: [row[::-1] for row in g]),
        ("flip_v", lambda g: g[::-1]),
        ("transpose", lambda g: list(zip(*g))),
    ]
    
    for i in range(count):
        h = rng.integers(3, 6)
        w = rng.integers(3, 6)
        grid = [[rng.integers(0, 2) for _ in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]
        
        # Compose 2 transforms
        t1_name, t1_fn = rng.choice(transforms)
        t2_name, t2_fn = rng.choice(transforms)
        
        try:
            intermediate = t1_fn(grid)
            intermediate = [list(row) for row in intermediate]
            result = t2_fn(intermediate)
            result = [list(row) for row in result]
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        grid_str = ' '.join(''.join(str(v) for v in row) for row in grid)
        result_str = ' '.join(''.join(str(v) for v in row) for row in result)
        
        cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(
            problem=f"Q: Transform grid with {t1_name} then {t2_name}: {grid_str}\nA:",
            target=result_str,
            domain="arc_grid",
            difficulty=4,
            generalization_type="compositional",
            metadata={"transforms": [t1_name, t2_name]}
        ))
    
    return cases


def generate_reordered_objects(seed: int, count: int = 50) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate tasks with reordered objects/operands."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cases = []
    
    for i in range(count):
        a, b = rng.integers(1, 1000, 2)
        op = rng.choice(['+', '-', '*', '/'])
        
        if op == '+':
            ans = a + b
            # Test commutativity: b + a
            problem = f"Q: Calculate {b} + {a}.\nA:"
        elif op == '*':
            ans = a * b
            problem = f"Q: Calculate {b} * {a}.\nA:"
        elif op == '-':
            ans = a - b
            # Test non-commutativity awareness
            problem = f"Q: Calculate {b} - {a}.\nA:"
            ans = b - a
        else:  # division
            if b != 0:
                ans = a // b
                problem = f"Q: Calculate {b} / {a}.\nA:"
                ans = b // a if a != 0 else 0
            else:
                continue
        
        cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(
            problem=problem,
            target=str(ans),
            domain="arithmetic",
            difficulty=2,
            generalization_type="reordered_objects",
            metadata={"original": f"{a} {op} {b}", "commutative": op in ['+', '*']}
        ))
    
    return cases

    """Generate tasks with irrelevant distractor information."""

def generate_longer_sequences(seed: int, count: int = 50) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate longer reasoning sequences than training."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cases = []
    
    for i in range(count):
        # Multi-step arithmetic chain
        steps = rng.integers(4, 8)  # Training: 1-3 steps
        vals = [rng.integers(1, 20)]
        ops = []
        
        for _ in range(steps):
            op = rng.choice(['+', '-', '*'])
            val = rng.integers(1, 20)
            ops.append(op)
            if op == '+':
                vals.append(vals[-1] + val)
            elif op == '-':
                vals.append(vals[-1] - val)
            else:
                vals.append(vals[-1] * val)
        
        # Build problem
        expr = str(vals[0])
        for op, v in zip(ops, vals[1:]):
            expr += f" {op} {v}"
        
        problem = f"Q: Calculate {expr}.\nA:"
        
        cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(
            problem=problem,
            target=str(vals[-1]),
            domain="arithmetic",
            difficulty=4,
            generalization_type="longer_sequences",
            metadata={"steps": steps, "expression": expr}
        ))
    
    return cases


def generate_unseen_tool_combinations(seed: int, count: int = 30) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate tool use with unseen tool combinations."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cases = []
    
    # Training: single tool calls; Test: multi-tool chains
    for i in range(count):
        # Chain: calculator -> file_write
        a, b = rng.integers(1, 100, 2)
        op = rng.choice(['+', '-', '*'])
        if op == '+':
            calc_result = a + b
        elif op == '-':
            calc_result = a - b
        else:
            calc_result = a * b
        
        problem = f"Q: Calculate {a} {op} {b} and write the result to /tmp/out.txt.\nA:"
        
        # Expected: two tool calls
        cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(
            problem=problem,
            target=f"Multi-step: calculator then file_write",
            domain="tool_use",
            difficulty=4,
            generalization_type="unseen_tool_combinations",
            metadata={"tools": ["calculator", "file_write"], "chain": True}
        ))
    
    return cases

# Master held-out generator

def generate_all_heldout(
    seed: int = 42,
    cases_per_type: int = 50
) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Generate all held-out generalization test cases."""
    all_cases = []
    
    generators = [
        ("unseen_numbers", generate_unseen_numbers),
        ("unseen_grid_properties", generate_unseen_grid_properties),
        ("compositional", generate_compositional_generalization),
        ("reordered_objects", generate_reordered_objects),
        ("distractors", generate_distractor_objects),
        ("longer_sequences", generate_longer_sequences),
        ("unseen_tool_combinations", generate_unseen_tool_combinations),
    ]
    
    for i, (name, gen_fn) in enumerate(generators):
        cases = gen_fn(seed + i * 1000, cases_per_type)
        for c in cases:
            c.metadata["generalization_type"] = name
        all_cases.extend(cases)
        print(f"  {name}: {len(cases)} cases")
    
    # Shuffle
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 99999)
    rng.shuffle(all_cases)
    
    return all_cases


def save_heldout(cases: List[GeneralizationTestCase], path: str) -> None:
    """Save held-out cases to JSONL."""
    with open(path, 'w') as f:
        for c in cases:
            d = asdict(c)
            # Convert numpy types
            def convert(obj):
                if isinstance(obj, (np.integer,)):
                    return int(obj)
                if isinstance(obj, (np.floating,)):
                    return float(obj)
                if isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
                    return obj.tolist()
                if isinstance(obj, dict):
                    return {k: convert(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
                if isinstance(obj, list):
                    return [convert(v) for v in obj]
                return obj
            f.write(json.dumps(convert(d)) + '\n')


def load_heldout(path: str) -> List[GeneralizationTestCase]:
    """Load held-out cases from JSONL."""
    cases = []
    with open(path, 'r') as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.strip():
                data = json.loads(line)
                cases.append(GeneralizationTestCase(**data))
    return cases


# --------------------------------------------------
# Evaluation

def evaluate_generalization(
    cases: List[GeneralizationTestCase],
    model_fn: Callable[[str], str],
    tokenizer: Optional[Any] = None,
    reasoning_format_available: bool = True
) -> Tuple[List[GeneralizationResult], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Evaluate model on held-out generalization cases.
    
    Args:
        cases: Held-out test cases
        model_fn: Function that takes prompt and returns model output
        tokenizer: Optional tokenizer for parsing structured output
        reasoning_format_available: Whether reasoning_format module is available
    
    Returns:
        List of results and summary statistics
    """
    results = []
    
    for case in cases:
        import time
        start = time.perf_counter()
        
        model_output = model_fn(case.problem)
        
        latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        
        # Parse structured reasoning if available
        parsed_reasoning = None
        structured_valid = False
        verification_passed = False
        
        if reasoning_format_available and case.structured:
            try:
                parsed_reasoning = parse_structured_reasoning(model_output)
                is_valid, _ = validate_structured_reasoning(model_output)
                structured_valid = is_valid
                
                if parsed_reasoning.verify:
                    verification_passed = "PASS" in parsed_reasoning.verify.upper()
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        # Check exact match
        exact_match = model_output.strip() == case.target.strip()
        
        # Check partial match (answer contained)
        if case.structured and parsed_reasoning and parsed_reasoning.answer:
            partial_match = case.target.strip() in parsed_reasoning.answer or \
                           parsed_reasoning.answer.strip() in case.target.strip()
        else:
            partial_match = case.target.strip() in model_output
        
        results.append(GeneralizationResult(
            test_case=case,
            model_output=model_output,
            parsed_reasoning=parsed_reasoning,
            exact_match=exact_match,
            partial_match=partial_match,
            structured_valid=structured_valid,
            verification_passed=verification_passed,
            latency_ms=latency_ms
        ))
    
    # Summary statistics
    summary = {
        "total_cases": len(cases),
        "exact_match_rate": sum(r.exact_match for r in results) / len(results),
        "partial_match_rate": sum(r.partial_match for r in results) / len(results),
        "structured_valid_rate": sum(r.structured_valid for r in results) / len(results),
        "verification_passed_rate": sum(r.verification_passed for r in results) / len(results),
        "avg_latency_ms": np.mean([r.latency_ms for r in results]),
        "by_generalization_type": {},
        "by_domain": {},
    }
    
    # Break down by generalization type
    by_type: Dict[str, List[GeneralizationResult]] = {}
    for r in results:
        gtype = r.test_case.generalization_type
        by_type.setdefault(gtype, []).append(r)
    
    for gtype, type_results in by_type.items():
        summary["by_generalization_type"][gtype] = {
            "count": len(type_results),
            "exact_match_rate": sum(r.exact_match for r in type_results) / len(type_results),
            "partial_match_rate": sum(r.partial_match for r in type_results) / len(type_results),
        }
    
    # Break down by domain
    by_domain: Dict[str, List[GeneralizationResult]] = {}
    for r in results:
        domain = r.test_case.domain
        by_domain.setdefault(domain, []).append(r)
    
    for domain, domain_results in by_domain.items():
        summary["by_domain"][domain] = {
            "count": len(domain_results),
            "exact_match_rate": sum(r.exact_match for r in domain_results) / len(domain_results),
        }
    
    return results, summary


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Generate held-out cases
    print("Generating held-out generalization cases...")
    cases = generate_all_heldout(seed=42, cases_per_type=20)
    print(f"Total cases: {len(cases)}")
    
    # Save
    save_heldout(cases, "/tmp/heldout_generalization.jsonl")
    print("Saved to /tmp/heldout_generalization.jsonl")
    
    # Print summary by type
    from collections import Counter
    types = Counter(c.generalization_type for c in cases)
    for t, count in types.items():
        print("  " + t + ": " + str(count))
