class TestPermissionModel:
    """Tests for plugin permission model."""

    def test_sensitive_permissions_defined(self):
        """Test that sensitive permissions are correctly identified."""
        model = PluginPermissionModel()
        
        # These should be sensitive
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.SHELL.value)
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.PROCESS_EXECUTION.value)
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.FILESYSTEM_WRITE.value)
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.SECRETS.value)
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.MICROPHONE.value)
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.CAMERA.value)
        assert model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.AUTOMATION.value)

        # These should NOT be sensitive (auto-granted)
        assert not model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.FILESYSTEM_READ.value)
        assert not model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.NETWORK.value)
        assert not model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.SYSTEM_INFO.value)
        assert not model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.BROWSER.value)
        assert not model.is_sensitive(PluginPermission.CLIPBOARD.value)

    def test_approval_flow(self):
        """Test permission approval flow."""
        model = PluginPermissionModel()
        plugin_id = "test.plugin"
        version = "1.0.0"
        permission = PluginPermission.SHELL.value

        # Initially not granted
        assert not model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, permission)

        # Request approval
        approval = model.request_approval(plugin_id, version, permission)
        assert approval.status == ApprovalStatus.PENDING

        # Grant approval
        assert model.grant_approval(plugin_id, version, permission)
        assert model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, permission)

        # Revoke approval
        assert model.revoke_approval(plugin_id, version, permission)
        assert not model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, permission)

    def test_deny_approval(self):
        """Test denying a permission."""
        model = PluginPermissionModel()
        plugin_id = "test.plugin"
        version = "1.0.0"
        permission = PluginPermission.SECRETS.value

        model.request_approval(plugin_id, version, permission)
        assert model.deny_approval(plugin_id, version, permission)
        
        approval = model.get_approval(plugin_id, version, permission)
        assert approval.status == ApprovalStatus.DENIED

    def test_permission_independence(self):
        """Test that permissions are independent - NETWORK doesn't grant SHELL."""
        model = PluginPermissionModel()
        plugin_id = "test.plugin"
        version = "1.0.0"

        # Grant NETWORK
        model.grant_approval(plugin_id, version, PluginPermission.NETWORK.value)
        assert model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, PluginPermission.NETWORK.value)

        # SHELL should still not be granted
        assert not model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, PluginPermission.SHELL.value)

    def test_version_change_invalidates_approvals(self):
        """Test that plugin version change invalidates old approvals."""
        model = PluginPermissionModel()
        plugin_id = "test.plugin"
        old_version = "1.0.0"
        new_version = "1.1.0"

        # Grant approvals for old version
        for perm in [PluginPermission.SHELL.value, PluginPermission.SECRETS.value]:
            model.grant_approval(plugin_id, old_version, perm)

        # Check permission set changed
        new_perms = model.check_permission_set_changed(
            plugin_id, old_version, new_version,
            [PluginPermission.SHELL.value, PluginPermission.SECRETS.value],
            [PluginPermission.SHELL.value, PluginPermission.SECRETS.value, PluginPermission.FILESYSTEM_WRITE.value],
        )

        # Old approvals should be revoked
        assert not model.is_granted(plugin_id, old_version, PluginPermission.SHELL.value)
        assert not model.is_granted(plugin_id, old_version, PluginPermission.SECRETS.value)
        
        # New sensitive permission should be requested
        assert PluginPermission.FILESYSTEM_WRITE.value in new_perms

    def test_no_allow_everything_forever(self):
        """Test that 'allow everything forever' is not the default for sensitive permissions."""
        import tempfile
        from pathlib import Path
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json', delete=False) as tmp:
            temp_path = Path(tmp.name)
        try:
            model = PluginPermissionModel(approvals_store=temp_path)
            plugin_id = "test.plugin"
            version = "1.0.0"

            # By default, sensitive permissions should NOT be granted
            for perm in PluginPermission:
                if model.is_sensitive(perm.value):
                    assert not model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, perm.value), f"{perm.value} should not be granted by default"
            
            # Non-sensitive permissions ARE auto-granted (by design)
            for perm in PluginPermission:
                if not model.is_sensitive(perm.value):
                    assert model.is_granted(plugin_id, version, perm.value), f"{perm.value} should be auto-granted"
        finally:
            temp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

class StubModels:
    """Hermetic ModelManager stand-in with a fixed inventory."""

    def __init__(self, models=None, default="mid-1b", calls=None):
        self._models = list(models if models is not None else [
            {"id": "tiny-100m", "provider": "builtin", "size": 100,
             "thinking": False, "context": 2048, "capabilities": ["chat"]},
            {"id": "mid-1b", "provider": "builtin", "size": 1000,
             "thinking": False, "context": 4096, "capabilities": ["chat"]},
            {"id": "big-8b", "provider": "ollama", "size": 8000,
             "thinking": True, "context": 8192, "capabilities": ["chat"]},
        ])
        self.default_model = default
        self.provider_pref = "auto"
        self.calls = calls if calls is not None else []

    def inventory_for_controller(self):
        return self._models

    def generate(self, prompt, model=None, timeout_s=None, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append({"prompt": prompt, "model": model,
                           "timeout_s": timeout_s, "kwargs": kwargs})
        if timeout_s is not None and timeout_s <= 0:
            raise TimeoutError("budget exhausted")
        return f"answer[{model}]"


class ControllerStub(AdaptiveReasoningController):
    def inventory(self):
        return list(self.models.inventory_for_controller())


def _controller(**kwargs):
    return ControllerStub(StubModels(**kwargs))

from __future__ import annotations
"""Natural-language reference resolution tests (v1.1 upgrade layer).

Covers: file reference, previous-step output, "it", "that file",
"read it back", ambiguous, nonexistent, unverified output,
sandbox/traversal, multi-step chain, voice transcript, conversation
isolation. Uses the real resolver + real Brain pipeline (in-memory
stores); no microphone required.
"""

import os

import pytest

from cognition.planner.capable import build_capable_plan
from cognition.planner.references import (
    ReferenceResolutionError,
    extract_file_mentions,
    resolve_plan_references,
    resolve_step_texts,
    split_compound_steps,
)


def _plan(texts):
    return build_capable_plan("g", list(texts), chain=True)


# 1. file reference
def test_1_file_reference():
    resolved, report = resolve_step_texts(["Create test.py", "Read that file"])
    assert resolved[1] == "Read test.py"
    assert report["ok"] is True


# 2. previous-step output reference (file output)
def test_2_previous_step_output_reference():
    plan = _plan(["Create test.py", "Use the result"])
    resolved, report = resolve_plan_references(plan)
    assert report["ok"] is True
    assert "test.py" in resolved[1]["description"]


# 3. "it"
def test_3_it_resolves_to_single_candidate():
    resolved, _ = resolve_step_texts(["Create test.py", "Read it"])
    assert resolved[1] == "Read test.py"


# 4. "that file"
def test_4_that_file():
    plan = _plan(["Create test.py", "Open that file"])
    resolved, _ = resolve_plan_references(plan)
    assert "test.py" in resolved[1]["description"]
    assert "that file" not in resolved[1]["description"].lower()


# 5. "read it back"
def test_5_read_it_back():
    resolved, _ = resolve_step_texts(
        ["Create test.py with hello", "Read it back"])
    assert resolved[1] == "Read test.py back"


# 6. ambiguous reference (never guess, no execution)
def test_6_ambiguous_reference_lists_candidates():
    with pytest.raises(ReferenceResolutionError) as excinfo:
        resolve_step_texts(["Create a.py", "Create b.py", "Read it"])
    assert excinfo.value.code == "AMBIGUOUS_REFERENCE"
    assert set(excinfo.value.candidates) == {"a.py", "b.py"}


# 7. nonexistent reference
def test_7_nonexistent_reference():
    with pytest.raises(ReferenceResolutionError) as excinfo:
        resolve_step_texts(["Read it"])
    assert excinfo.value.code == "UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE"


# 8. reference to unverified output
def test_8_unverified_output_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ReferenceResolutionError) as excinfo:
        resolve_step_texts(
            ["Read it"],
            context={"unverified_artifacts": ["test.py"]})
    assert excinfo.value.code == "UNVERIFIED_REFERENCE"


# 9. sandbox / path traversal attempt
def test_9_traversal_reference_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ReferenceResolutionError) as excinfo:
        resolve_step_texts(
            ["Read it"],
            context={"verified_artifacts": ["../evil.txt"]})
    assert excinfo.value.code == "REFERENCE_SANDBOX_VIOLATION"


# 10. multi-step reference chain
def test_10_multi_step_chain():
    goal = "Create test.py, write a program in it, then read it back."
    from cognition.planner.capable import decompose_goal
    parts = decompose_goal(goal)
    split = split_compound_steps(parts)
    assert len(split) == 3
    resolved, _ = resolve_step_texts(split)
    assert resolved[0] == "Create test.py"
    assert "test.py" in resolved[1]
    assert "test.py" in resolved[2]
    plan = build_capable_plan(goal, resolved, chain=True)
    rplan, _ = resolve_plan_references(plan)
    assert all("test.py" in s["description"] for s in rplan)

# 12. normal conversation isolation (no references, no error)
def test_12_normal_conversation_untouched():
    resolved, report = resolve_step_texts(
        ["What is your name?", "Hi HERCULE"])
    assert resolved == ["What is your name?", "Hi HERCULE"]
    assert report["code"] == "NO_REFERENCES"
    assert extract_file_mentions("What is your name?") == []


# 12b. regression: determiner prose ("this topic") is not an anaphor.
# "Research this topic" must plan and complete, never fail with
# UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE (bare this/that before a content noun is prose).
def test_12b_determiner_prose_never_aborts_plan():
    plan = _plan(["Research this topic"])
    resolved, report = resolve_plan_references(plan)
    assert report["ok"] is True
    assert resolved[0]["description"] == "Research this topic"
    resolved_texts, report2 = resolve_step_texts(["Research this topic"])
    assert resolved_texts == ["Research this topic"]
    assert report2["code"] == "NO_REFERENCES"
    # Verb-less chatter ("it is raining") is likewise prose.
    resolved3, _ = resolve_step_texts(["it is raining today"])
    assert resolved3 == ["it is raining today"]
    # But true task anaphora still requires an antecedent.
    with pytest.raises(ReferenceResolutionError) as excinfo:
        resolve_step_texts(["run it"])
    assert excinfo.value.code == "UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE"

def test_interrupted_task_recovers_without_replay(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    mock_env(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    from runtime.initializer import RuntimeInitializer
    from autonomy.worker import AutonomyWorker
    services = RuntimeInitializer().initialize()
    worker = AutonomyWorker(services, config={"poll_interval_s": 0.05})
    try:
        scheduled = worker.schedule("calculate 11+11")
        worker.start(recover=False)
        deadline = time.perf_counter() + 20.0
        while time.perf_counter() < deadline:
            if str(worker.tasks.get(scheduled["task_id"]).get("status")) == "COMPLETED":
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        before = dict(worker.tasks.get(scheduled["task_id"]))
        # Simulated restart over the same store.
        services2 = RuntimeInitializer().initialize()
        worker2 = AutonomyWorker(services2, config={"poll_interval_s": 0.05})
        try:
            summary = worker2.recover_on_startup()
            assert summary["resumed"] == []
            after = services2["orchestrator"].task_manager.get(scheduled["task_id"])
            assert str(after.get("status")) == "COMPLETED"
            assert before["metadata"].get("capability_states") == \
                after["metadata"].get("capability_states")
        finally:
            worker2.stop()
    finally:
        worker.stop()

class EchoAbility(BaseAbility):
    def __init__(self, name="echo", result="ok-content"):
        super().__init__(name, f"test {name}")
        self.calls = 0
        self.result = result

    def execute(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        return {"status": "success", "content": self.result}


class AlwaysFailAbility(BaseAbility):
    def __init__(self, name="always-fail"):
        super().__init__(name, "always fails")
        self.calls = 0

    def execute(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        raise RuntimeError("simulated persistent failure")


class FlapOnceAbility(BaseAbility):
    """Fails once, then succeeds: exercises genuine recovery via replan."""

    def __init__(self, name="flap-once"):
        super().__init__(name, "fails once then recovers")
        self.calls = 0

    def execute(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        if self.calls == 1:
            raise RuntimeError("simulated transient failure")
        return {"status": "success", "content": "recovered-content"}


class HighRiskAbility(BaseAbility):
    def __init__(self, name="danger-stub"):
        super().__init__(name, "high risk stub", risk="HIGH",
                         permissions=["TERMINAL_EXECUTE"])
        self.calls = 0

    def execute(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        return {"status": "success", "content": "should never run unapproved"}


def make_world(extra_abilities=(), max_replans=2, max_step_retries=1,
               time_budget=None):
    policy = PolicyManager()
    abilities = AbilityManager(policy)
    abilities.register(EchoAbility("files-stub"))
    abilities.register(EchoAbility("calc-stub", result="42"))
    for ability in extra_abilities:
        abilities.register(ability)
    registry = CapabilityRegistry()
    registry.register_provider("FILE_READ", "tool", "files-stub",
                               ability_manager=abilities)
    registry.register_provider("MATH", "tool", "calc-stub",
                               ability_manager=abilities)
    matcher = ToolMatcher(abilities, policy, None, registry)
    planner = Planner()
    tasks = TaskManager()
    tracer = Tracer()
    kwargs = {"max_replans": max_replans, "max_step_retries": max_step_retries}
    if time_budget is not None:
        kwargs["max_total_execution_time"] = time_budget
    loop = AutonomousLoop(planner, matcher, tasks, tracer, **kwargs)
    return abilities, policy, registry, matcher, planner, tasks, tracer, loop

class EchoAbility(BaseAbility):
    def __init__(self, name="echo", result="ok-content"):
        super().__init__(name, f"test {name}")
        self.calls = 0
        self.result = result

    def execute(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        return {"status": "success", "content": self.result}


class ScriptedModel:
    """Deterministic model double: canned outputs or raised errors."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        self.script = list(script)
        self.calls = []

    def generate(self, prompt, model=None, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append(prompt)
        item = self.script[min(len(self.calls) - 1, len(self.script) - 1)]
        if isinstance(item, Exception):
            raise item
        return item

    def route_for_purpose(self, purpose, **kwargs):
        return ("scripted", "mock", self)


def make_world(extra_abilities=()):

    abilities = AbilityManager(policy)
    abilities.register(EchoAbility("files-stub"))

    for ability in extra_abilities:
        abilities.register(ability)
    registry = CapabilityRegistry()
    registry.register_provider("FILE_READ", "tool", "files-stub",
                               ability_manager=abilities)
    registry.register_provider("MATH", "tool", "calc-stub",
                               ability_manager=abilities)
    matcher = ToolMatcher(abilities, policy, None, registry)
    planner = Planner()
    tasks = TaskManager()
    tracer = Tracer()
    loop = AutonomousLoop(planner, matcher, tasks, tracer)
    return abilities, policy, registry, matcher, planner, tasks, tracer, loop

"""Phase F: autonomy-level integration (UAI §27).

Levels gate *scheduling authority*; PolicyManager gates *operation
permission*. These tests prove the separation across all six levels
without running models: gate matrix, worker schedule enforcement,
policy independence, level-5 boundedness, and lifecycle ops.
"""

import threading

import pytest

from autonomy.levels import (
    LEVEL_MAX_RISK,
    LEVEL_MAX_RUNTIME_S,
    LEVEL_NAMES,
    RISK_ORDER,
    classify_goal_risk,
    evaluate_gate,
    normalize_level,
)
from autonomy.worker import AutonomyWorker

LOW_GOAL = "read the project notes"
MEDIUM_GOAL = "create a summary report"
HIGH_GOAL = "delete temp folders"


def _bare_worker(level):
    """Lightweight worker: gate + lifecycle only, no runtime/services."""
    worker = AutonomyWorker.__new__(AutonomyWorker)
    worker.services = {}
    worker.brain = type("B", (), {"consciousness": None, "event_bus": None})()
    worker.tasks = _StubTasks()
    worker.enabled = True
    worker.autonomy_level = normalize_level(level)
    worker.scheduler = None
    worker._owns_scheduler = False
    worker._stop_event = threading.Event()
    worker._paused = False
    worker._lock = threading.Lock()
    worker._future = None
    worker._worker_state = "STOPPED"
    worker._active_task_id = None
    worker._last_result = None
    worker.max_task_runtime_s = 60.0
    worker.max_concurrent_tasks = 1
    worker._started_count = 0
    worker._completed_count = 0
    worker._failed_count = 0
    return worker


class _StubTasks:
    def __init__(self):
        self._tasks = {}
        self._seq = 0

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._tasks.values())

    def create_task(self, goal, timeout=60, metadata=None, priority=5):
        self._seq += 1
        tid = f"t-{self._seq}"
        self._tasks[tid] = {"id": tid, "goal": goal, "status": "CREATED",
                            "metadata": dict(metadata or {})}
        return tid

    def get(self, tid):
        return self._tasks[tid]

    def queue_task(self, tid):
        self._tasks[tid]["status"] = "QUEUED"

    def save(self):
        pass


# ---------- gate matrix: all six levels ----------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("level,low,medium,high", [
    (0, False, False, False),
    (1, False, False, False),
    (2, True, True, False),
    (3, True, True, False),
    (4, True, True, True),
    (5, True, True, True),
])
def test_gate_matrix_all_levels(level, low, medium, high):
    assert evaluate_gate(level, LOW_GOAL)["allowed"] is low
    assert evaluate_gate(level, MEDIUM_GOAL)["allowed"] is medium
    assert evaluate_gate(level, HIGH_GOAL)["allowed"] is high


def test_gate_reasons_name_level_and_risk():

def test_gate_deterministic_and_ceiling_shape():

    assert set(LEVEL_MAX_RISK) == {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
    assert set(LEVEL_NAMES) == {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
    assert set(RISK_ORDER) == {"LOW", "MEDIUM", "HIGH"}


# ---------- worker schedule enforcement per level ----------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("level,expect", [(0, False), (1, False), (2, True)])
def test_worker_schedule_low_goal_by_level(level, expect):
    worker = _bare_worker(level)
    if expect:

    for level in (0, 1, 2, 3):

            _bare_worker(level).schedule(HIGH_GOAL)
    out = _bare_worker(5).schedule(HIGH_GOAL)

# ---------- policy independence: level never overrides denial ----------

def test_high_level_does_not_bypass_policy():
    from security.permissions.policy_manager import PolicyManager

    policy = PolicyManager()
    # Gate at level 5 allows the HIGH-risk goal to be scheduled...
    assert evaluate_gate(5, HIGH_GOAL)["allowed"] is True
    out = _bare_worker(5).schedule(HIGH_GOAL)
    assert out["status"] == "QUEUED"
    # ...but PolicyManager still denies the operation independently.
    policy.set_permission("FILE_WRITE", False)
    try:
        decision = policy.evaluate("FILE_WRITE", {"risk": "HIGH"})
        assert decision["allowed"] is False
    finally:
        policy.set_permission("FILE_WRITE", True)
    assert policy.evaluate("FILE_WRITE", {"risk": "HIGH"})["allowed"] is True

    policy = PolicyManager()
    assert policy.evaluate("NETWORK_ACCESS", {"risk": "MEDIUM"})["required_approval"] is True
    assert policy.evaluate("TERMINAL_EXECUTE", {"risk": "HIGH"})["required_approval"] is True
    assert policy.evaluate("FILE_READ", {"risk": "LOW"})["required_approval"] is False

    assert worker.resume()["state"] == "IDLE"

class FlakyAbility(BaseAbility):
    """Fails once, then succeeds — bounded replan/recovery."""

    def __init__(self, name="flaky-tool"):
        super().__init__(name, "flaky")
        self.calls = 0

    def execute(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        if self.calls == 1:
            return {"status": "failed", "error": "transient boom"}
        return {"status": "success", "content": "recovered-content"}


class DictSource:
    def __init__(self, sources=None, error=None):
        self._sources = sources
        self._error = error

    def execute(self, topic, **kwargs):
        if self._error is not None:
            raise self._error
        return {"status": "success", "sources": self._sources}

def wait_for(predicate, timeout=20.0, interval=0.05):
    deadline = time.perf_counter() + timeout
    while time.perf_counter() < deadline:
        if predicate():
            return True
        time.sleep(interval)
    return predicate()

from __future__ import annotations
"""Phase G: research integration (UAI §23).

ResearchAbility runs the real ResearchEngine workflow through the
ability pipeline. No network is touched: scripted source doubles
stand in for web/search abilities. Honesty rules are absolute —
unreachable/empty/malformed sources yield ``unverified`` + ``[]``.
"""

import pytest

from abilities.ability_manager import AbilityManager
from abilities.research.research_ability import ResearchAbility
from security.permissions.policy_manager import PolicyManager


class _DictSource:
    """Scripted source double returning a fixed sources envelope."""

    def __init__(self, sources=None, error=None):
        self._sources = sources
        self._error = error

    def execute(self, topic, **kwargs):
        if self._error is not None:
            raise self._error
        return {"status": "success", "sources": self._sources}


def _manager_with_research(source=None):
    policy = PolicyManager()
    abilities = AbilityManager(policy)
    abilities.register(ResearchAbility(source_ability=source))
    return abilities, policy


# 1. research request without a source is honest
def test_request_without_source_is_unverified():
    ability = ResearchAbility()
    out = ability.execute("anything at all")
    assert out["status"] == "success"  # workflow ran
    assert out["verification_status"] == "unverified"
    assert out["evidence"] == []
    assert out["sources"] == []
    assert out["error"] is None  # honest-success path: no failure occurred
    assert "no source material" in out["synthesis"].lower()


# 2. source discovery / late wiring
def test_attach_source_wires_discovery():
    ability = ResearchAbility()
    assert ability.execute("t")["evidence"] == []
    ability.attach_source(_DictSource(
        [{"url": "https://example.test/a", "content": "[FACT] alpha holds"}]))
    out = ability.execute("t")
    assert len(out["evidence"]) == 1
    assert out["sources"] == ["https://example.test/a"]


# 3. successful source collects labeled evidence
def test_successful_source_labels():
    ability = ResearchAbility(_DictSource([
        {"url": "u1", "content": "[FACT] Water boils at 100C at sea level"},
        {"url": "u2", "content": "Therefore the sample will boil near 100C"},
    ]))
    out = ability.execute("boiling point")
    assert out["status"] == "success"
    labels = [e["label"] for e in out["evidence"]]
    assert labels == ["FACT", "INFERENCE"]
    assert out["synthesis"] and "FACT" in out["synthesis"]


# 4. unavailable network (source raises) -> unverified, no fabrication
def test_unavailable_network_is_honest():
    ability = ResearchAbility(_DictSource(error=ConnectionError("offline")))
    out = ability.execute("anything")
    assert out["verification_status"] == "unverified"
    assert out["evidence"] == []
    assert out["sources"] == []


# 5. malformed source envelope -> unverified, no fabrication
def test_malformed_source_is_honest():
    class _Garbage:
        def execute(self, topic, **kwargs):
            return {"unexpected": object()}

    out = ResearchAbility(_Garbage()).execute("anything")
    assert out["verification_status"] == "unverified"
    assert out["evidence"] == []


# 6. empty result -> unverified
def test_empty_result_is_honest():
    out = ResearchAbility(_DictSource([])).execute("nothing to find")
    assert out["verification_status"] == "unverified"
    assert out["evidence"] == []
    assert "no source material" in out["synthesis"].lower()


# 7. multiple sources all surface with provenance
def test_multiple_sources_keep_provenance():
    ability = ResearchAbility(_DictSource([
        {"url": "a", "content": "[FACT] first claim here"},
        {"url": "b", "content": "[FACT] second claim here"},
        {"url": "c", "content": "plain unmarked material"},
    ]))
    out = ability.execute("topic")
    assert [e["source"] for e in out["evidence"]] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert out["sources"] == ["a", "b", "c"]


# 8. conflicting evidence is flagged, never silently merged
def test_conflicting_evidence_flagged():
    ability = ResearchAbility(_DictSource([
        {"url": "doc-a", "content": "[FACT] The library supports python 3.12"},
        {"url": "doc-b", "content": "[FACT] The library does not support python 3.12"},
    ]))
    out = ability.execute("compatibility")
    assert len(out["contradictions"]) == 1
    assert "doc-a" in out["contradictions"][0]
    assert out["verification_status"] == "unverified"  # contradictions block verified


# 9. verification semantics: 2+ clean facts verify, else not
def test_verification_semantics():
    clean = ResearchAbility(_DictSource([
        {"url": "a", "content": "[FACT] alpha element present here"},
        {"url": "b", "content": "[FACT] beta element present here"},
    ])).execute("t")
    assert clean["verification_status"] == "verified"
    assert clean["confidence"] > 0.5
    single = ResearchAbility(_DictSource(
        [{"url": "a", "content": "[FACT] lonely fact stated here"}])).execute("t")
    assert single["verification_status"] == "unverified"


# 10. ability-pipeline integration: policy + capabilities + validation
def test_pipeline_integration():
    abilities, policy = _manager_with_research()
    out = abilities.execute("research", "pipeline topic",
                            capabilities=["KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL"])
    assert out["status"] == "success"
    assert out["verification_status"] == "unverified"  # no source attached
    # Empty topics are rejected before execution.
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="Invalid inputs"):
        abilities.execute("research", "   ",
                          capabilities=["KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL"])
    # Policy denial is enforced at the pipeline, not bypassed by research.
    policy.set_permission("KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL", False)
    try:
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="Permission denied"):
            abilities.execute("research", "pipeline topic",
                              capabilities=["KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL"])
    finally:
        policy.set_permission("KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL", True)

def _math_tasks():
    from evaluation.framework.datasets.uai_core import uai_core_tasks

    return [t for t in uai_core_tasks()
            if t.task_id in ("uai-core-math-001", "uai-core-math-002")]


def test_evaluation_leaves_sentinel_untouched(tmp_path):
    from evaluation.framework.adapters import HermeticEvalAdapter
    from evaluation.framework.config import EvalConfig
    from evaluation.framework.runner import EvaluationRunner

    sentinel = tmp_path / "prod" / "experiences.json"
    sentinel.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"version": 1, "records": [{"experience_id": "sentinel-1"}]}
    sentinel.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")
    digest = sentinel.read_bytes()
    adapter = HermeticEvalAdapter()
    try:
        run = EvaluationRunner(adapter, EvalConfig(live=False)).run_suite(
            _math_tasks(), scope="sentinel")
        assert run.counts["passed"] == 2
        # Learning happened — inside evaluation state, not the sentinel.
        from pathlib import Path

        eval_records = json.loads(
            (Path(adapter.state_dir) / "memory" / "experiences.json").read_text(
                encoding="utf-8"))
        assert len(eval_records.get("records", [])) >= 2
    finally:
        adapter.close()
    assert sentinel.read_bytes() == digest


# ---------- cross-suite isolation (A-B-A determinism) ----------

def _run_scope(task_ids, scope):
    from evaluation.framework.adapters import HermeticEvalAdapter
    from evaluation.framework.config import EvalConfig
    from evaluation.framework.registry import suite_tasks
    from evaluation.framework.runner import EvaluationRunner

    pool = {t.task_id: t for sid in ("uai_core", "uai_research")
            for t in suite_tasks(sid)}
    tasks = [pool[tid] for tid in task_ids]
    adapter = HermeticEvalAdapter()
    try:
        run = EvaluationRunner(adapter, EvalConfig(live=False)).run_suite(
            tasks, scope=scope)
        return run, adapter.state_dir
    finally:
        adapter.close()


def test_cross_suite_isolation_aba():

    run_a1, dir_a1 = _run_scope(math_ids, "iso-a1")

    assert run_a1.counts == run_a2.counts
    assert [(r.task_id, r.outcome.value, r.score) for r in run_a1.results] == \
           [(r.task_id, r.outcome.value, r.score) for r in run_a2.results]

"""Phase E regression tests: timezone-aware UTC across the intelligence layer.

External format is preserved as ISO-8601 strings; the only intended change
vs the legacy naive UTC-now isoformat output is the
``+00:00`` UTC offset suffix. All internal datetime objects must be
timezone-aware so that arithmetic/comparison never raises::

    TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone

from cognition.task_manager.task_manager import TaskManager
from intelligence.coordination.coordinator_metrics import CoordinatorMetrics
from intelligence.coordination.coordinator_state import CoordinatorStateManager
from intelligence.coordination.execution_graph import ExecutionGraph

from intelligence.runtime.execution_state import ExecutionState
from intelligence.runtime.runtime_cache import RuntimeCache
from intelligence.runtime.runtime_metrics import RuntimeMetrics
from intelligence.runtime.runtime_monitor import RuntimeMonitor
from intelligence.world_model import WorldModel


def _assert_aware_iso(ts: str):
    parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
    assert parsed.tzinfo is not None, f"naive timestamp: {ts!r}"
    assert parsed.utcoffset() is not None, f"missing utcoffset: {ts!r}"
    return parsed


def test_world_model_timestamps_are_timezone_aware():
    model = WorldModel(kernel=None)
    model.add_relationship("A", "knows", "B")
    payload = model.process({})
    first = _assert_aware_iso(payload["timestamp"])
    assert first.tzinfo is not None
    rel_ts = _assert_aware_iso(model.relationships[0]["timestamp"])
    # UTC semantics preserved: offset must be zero.
    assert first.utcoffset().total_seconds() == 0
    assert rel_ts.utcoffset().total_seconds() == 0


def test_runtime_cache_and_monitor_keep_aware_utc_timestamps():
    cache = RuntimeCache()
    cache.put("demo", "value", ttl=60)
    assert cache.get("demo") == "value"

    monitor = RuntimeMonitor()
    monitor.record("test.event", {"result": "ok"})
    event = monitor.events[0]
    _assert_aware_iso(event["timestamp"])

    metrics = RuntimeMetrics()
    metrics.record(0.25, success=True)
    _assert_aware_iso(metrics.report()["started"])


def test_runtime_cache_expiry_uses_aware_comparison():
    cache = RuntimeCache()
    cache.put("short", "v", ttl=100)
    entry = cache.cache["short"]
    assert entry.created.tzinfo is not None
    assert entry.expires.tzinfo is not None
    # Must not raise TypeError: aware vs aware comparison.
    assert entry.expired in (True, False)
    assert cache.get("short") == "v"

    cache.put("neg", "gone", ttl=-1)
    assert cache.get("neg") is None

def test_execution_state_lifecycle_stays_aware():
    state = ExecutionState()
    assert state.created.tzinfo is not None
    state.start()
    state.complete()
    assert state.started.tzinfo is not None
    assert state.finished.tzinfo is not None
    # Aware minus aware must not raise.
    duration = (state.finished - state.started).total_seconds()
    assert duration >= 0
    stats = state.statistics()
    _assert_aware_iso(stats["created"])
    _assert_aware_iso(stats["started"])
    _assert_aware_iso(stats["finished"])
    assert stats["duration"] is not None

    assert manager.updated >= manager.created  # no TypeError
    for item in manager.history():
        _assert_aware_iso(item["timestamp"])

    _assert_aware_iso(stats["created"])
    _assert_aware_iso(stats["updated"])

def test_timestamp_ordering_and_serialization_roundtrip():
    monitor = RuntimeMonitor()
    monitor.record("first", {})
    monitor.record("second", {})
    stamps = [_assert_aware_iso(e["timestamp"]) for e in monitor.events]
    assert stamps[1] >= stamps[0]
    # JSON-compatible strings survive a serialize/deserialize round trip.
    import json

    blob = json.dumps(monitor.events)

def test_no_naive_aware_mismatch_across_components():
    """Regression: mixing any two component timestamps must not raise TypeError."""
    cache = RuntimeCache()
    cache.put("k", "v", ttl=60)
    metrics = RuntimeMetrics()
    state_mgr = CoordinatorStateManager()
    state_mgr.start()
    candidates = [
        cache.cache["k"].created,
        cache.cache["k"].expires,
        metrics.started,
        state_mgr.created,
        state_mgr.updated,
        datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    ]
    for candidate in candidates:
        assert candidate.tzinfo is not None
    ordered = sorted(candidates)
    assert len(ordered) == len(candidates)
    for earlier, later in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
        assert (later - earlier).total_seconds() >= 0 or True  # comparison itself must not raise

def _png_1x1() -> bytes:
    def chunk(ctype: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        return (struct.pack(">I", len(payload)) + ctype + payload
                + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(ctype + payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF))

    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", 1, 1, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    raw = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
    return (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr)
            + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b"IEND", b""))

def test_tts_stop_interrupts_blocked_speech():
    # Regression: speak() must not hold the provider lock across the
    # blocking runAndWait(), or stop()/cancel() deadlocks against
    # in-flight speech (observed with SAPI5 and no audio device).
    from voice.text_to_speech import Pyttsx3TTS
    started = threading.Event()
    release = threading.Event()

    class BlockingEngine:
        def say(self, text):
            started.set()

        def runAndWait(self):
            release.wait(30)  # blocks like a device-less SAPI5 loop

        def stop(self):
            release.set()

    tts = Pyttsx3TTS()
    tts._engine = BlockingEngine()
    tts._probe = {"available": True, "engine": "test"}
    worker = threading.Thread(target=lambda: tts.speak("hello"), daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    assert started.wait(10)
    deadline = time.time() + 15
    assert tts.stop()["stopped"] is True  # must return, never deadlock
    assert time.time() < deadline
    worker.join(timeout=15)
    assert not worker.is_alive()

"""Web product tests (Phase 9L/9M): auth, isolation, rate limit, chat,
streaming, benchmark portal. Server binds loopback ephemeral port."""

import json
import threading
import urllib.request

import pytest

import web.server as srv


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def server():
    srv._sessions.clear()
    http = srv.run(port=0)
    port = http.server_address[1]
    thread = threading.Thread(target=http.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    http.shutdown()


def _req(base, path, token=None, data=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path,
                                 data=json.dumps(data).encode() if data else None,
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                                          **({"X-Auth-Token": token} if token else {})},
                                 method="POST" if data else "GET")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            return resp.status, resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        return exc.code, exc.read()


def test_public_pages_need_no_auth(server):
    for path in ("/", "/benchmarks", "/docs", "/safety", "/model-card"):
        code, _ = _req(server, path)
        assert code == 200, path

    code, _ = _req(server, "/api/reports/phase6_eval.json")

"""Tests for P1 Selected-Content Understanding: Workspace Policy Enforcement.

Tests cover:
1. No active workspace - access denied
2. Allowed in-workspace read/list
3. Relative traversal rejection (..)
4. Absolute-path escape rejection
5. Similar-prefix rejection (workspace-other/)
6. Nested allowed path
7. Sensitive-file rejection (.env, private keys)
8. Bounded read/truncation
9. Non-text/binary handling
10. Symlink/junction escape rejection
11. Read-only enforcement (no write via P1 path)
12. Consulted-file record privacy
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import tempfile
import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from workspace_manager import WorkspaceManager, create_workspace_manager, _is_sensitive_file, _matches_sensitive


class TestWorkspacePolicy:
    """Test suite for WorkspaceManager policy enforcement."""

    def setup_method(self):
        """Create a temporary workspace for each test."""
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.workspace = Path(self.temp_dir) / "workspace"
        self.workspace.mkdir(parents=True)
        
        # Create test files
        (self.workspace / "normal.txt").write_text("hello world")
        (self.workspace / "nested").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.workspace / "nested" / "deep.txt").write_text("deep content")
        
        # Create sensitive files
        (self.workspace / ".env").write_text("SECRET=123")
        (self.workspace / "id_rsa").write_text("fake private key")
        (self.workspace / "secret.key").write_text("secret")
        (self.workspace / "credentials.json").write_text('{"token": "abc"}')
        
        # Create a binary file
        (self.workspace / "binary.bin").write_bytes(b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\xff\xfe")
        
        # Create a large text file
        large_content = "x" * 10000
        (self.workspace / "large.txt").write_text(large_content)
        
        # Create outside workspace
        self.outside = Path(self.temp_dir) / "outside"
        self.outside.mkdir()
        (self.outside / "secret.txt").write_text("outside secret")
        
        # Create similar-prefix directory
        self.similar = Path(self.temp_dir) / "workspace-other"
        self.similar.mkdir()
        (self.similar / "file.txt").write_text("similar prefix")
        
        self.wm = WorkspaceManager()

    def teardown_method(self):
        """Clean up temp directory."""
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    # ================================================================
    # 1. No active workspace - access denied
    # ================================================================
    def test_no_active_workspace_denied(self):
        """Read/list with no selected workspace is denied."""
        wm = WorkspaceManager()
        
        # Read should be denied
        result = wm.read_file("normal.txt")
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "no_workspace"
        assert "no workspace selected" in result.reason.lower()
        
        # List should be denied
        result = wm.list_directory(".")
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "no_workspace"
        
        # No fallback to broad filesystem access
        assert result.denial_category == "no_workspace"

    # ================================================================
    # 2. Allowed in-workspace read/list
    # ================================================================
    def test_allowed_in_workspace_read(self):
        """Normal text file inside workspace can be read."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        result = self.wm.read_file("normal.txt")
        assert result.allowed
        assert result.workspace_relative == "normal.txt"
        assert "hello world" in result.path.read_text()
        
        # Consulted-file record created
        records = self.wm.get_consulted_files()
        assert len(records) == 1
        assert records[0].workspace_relative == "normal.txt"
        assert records[0].operation == "read"
        assert records[0].allowed is True

    def test_allowed_in_workspace_list(self):
        """Directory listing works within workspace."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        result = self.wm.list_directory(".")
        assert result.allowed
        # result.truncation contains item_count as int
        assert result.truncation.get("item_count", 0) > 0
        
        records = self.wm.get_consulted_files()
        assert any(r.operation == "list" for r in records)

    # ================================================================
    # 3. Relative traversal rejection (..)
    # ================================================================
    def test_relative_traversal_rejected(self):
        """Path traversal with .. is denied."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        result = self.wm.read_file("../outside/secret.txt")
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "traversal"
        assert "escapes workspace" in result.reason.lower()
        
        # Also test with nested path
        result = self.wm.read_file("nested/../../outside/secret.txt")
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "traversal"

    # ================================================================
    # 4. Absolute-path escape rejection
    # ================================================================
    def test_absolute_path_escape_rejected(self):
        """Absolute path outside workspace is denied."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        outside_file = str(self.outside / "secret.txt")
        result = self.wm.read_file(outside_file)
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "traversal"
        assert "escapes workspace" in result.reason.lower()

    # ================================================================
    # 5. Similar-prefix rejection (workspace-other/)
    # ================================================================
    def test_similar_prefix_rejected(self):
        """Sibling path like workspace-other/ is denied - proves no string-prefix check."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        # This would pass a naive string-prefix check but must fail proper containment
        similar_file = str(self.similar / "file.txt")
        result = self.wm.read_file(similar_file)
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "traversal"
        
        # Also test with relative path that looks like it might work
        # but actually goes outside
        result = self.wm.read_file("workspace-other/file.txt")
        assert not result.allowed

    # ================================================================
    # 6. Nested allowed path
    # ================================================================
    def test_nested_allowed_path(self):
        """Normal nested file inside workspace is allowed."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        result = self.wm.read_file("nested/deep.txt")
        assert result.allowed
        # Normalize path separators for cross-platform comparison
        import os
        expected = os.path.normpath("nested/deep.txt")
        assert os.path.normpath(result.workspace_relative) == expected
        assert "deep content" in result.path.read_text()

    # ================================================================
    # 7. Sensitive-file rejection
    # ================================================================
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("sensitive_file", [
        ".env",
        "id_rsa",
        "secret.key",
        "credentials.json",
    ])
    def test_sensitive_file_rejected(self, sensitive_file):
        """Sensitive files are denied before content is returned."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        result = self.wm.read_file(sensitive_file)
        assert not result.allowed
        assert result.denial_category == "sensitive_file"
        assert "sensitive" in result.reason.lower()
        
        # No content exposed
        records = self.wm.get_consulted_files()
        assert any(r.denial_category == "sensitive_file" for r in records)
        # Verify no content leaked in denial
        assert "SECRET" not in result.reason
        assert "private key" not in result.reason.lower()

    # ================================================================
    # 8. Bounded read/truncation
    # ================================================================
    def test_bounded_read_truncation_by_lines(self):
        """Large file is truncated at line limit with metadata."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        # Set low line limit
        self.wm.set_limits(max_lines=3)

    def test_bounded_read_truncation_by_chars(self):

        assert result.truncation.get("chars_read", 0) <= 50

    def test_bounded_read_truncation_by_size(self):
        """File exceeding size limit is rejected with metadata."""

        # Set very low size limit

        result = self.wm.read_file("large.txt")

        assert result.denial_category == "size_limit"
        assert result.truncation is not None

    # ================================================================
    # 9. Non-text/binary handling
    # ================================================================
    def test_binary_file_rejected(self):
        """Binary file is not treated as normal text."""

        result = self.wm.read_file("binary.bin")

    # ================================================================

    # ================================================================
    def test_readonly_enforcement_no_write_via_p1(self):
        """P1 read-only path exposes no write operation."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))

        # Write should fail in readonly mode
        result = ability.execute({"operation": "write", "path": "new.txt", "data": "test", "readonly": True})

    # ================================================================
    # 12. Consulted-file record privacy
    # ================================================================
    def test_consulted_file_record_privacy(self):
        """Denied sensitive reads don't log file contents."""
        self.wm.select_workspace(str(self.workspace))
        
        # Read sensitive file (denied)
        self.wm.read_file(".env")
        
        # Read normal file (allowed)
        self.wm.read_file("normal.txt")
        
        records = self.wm.get_consulted_files()
        
        # Check denied sensitive file record
        denied_record = next((r for r in records if r.denial_category == "sensitive_file"), None)
        assert denied_record is not None
        assert denied_record.allowed is False
        assert denied_record.denial_category == "sensitive_file"
        # No content leaked in denial reason
        assert "SECRET" not in denied_record.denial_reason
        assert "123" not in denied_record.denial_reason
        
        # Check allowed file record
        allowed_record = next((r for r in records if r.workspace_relative == "normal.txt"), None)
        assert allowed_record is not None
        assert allowed_record.allowed is True
        assert allowed_record.operation == "read"
        
        # Paths are workspace-relative, not absolute
        assert not os.path.isabs(allowed_record.workspace_relative)
        assert not os.path.isabs(denied_record.workspace_relative)
